chapters.title: Chapter 251 -251-Origin Essence, Earth Origin Access Unlocked
paragraphs: Daniel took out the Class Awakening Scroll and used it.
[Ding! The seal on your experience bar has been lifted. You may continue leveling up.]
Daniel did not hesitate and directly began leveling up.
[Ding! Your level has increased! Current level: 321. You have obtained 20 attribute points.]
[Ding! Your level has increased! Current level: 330. You have obtained 20 attribute points.]
[Ding! Your level has increased! Current level: 340. You have obtained 20 attribute points.]

[Notice: You have not yet completed the next stage of your class change. Your level cap has been sealed again. Excess experience has been temporarily stored in the Exp Pool. Please complete your class change as soon as possible to lift the cap.]
Level 340!
Daniel was thoroughly satisfied and soon returned to Earth.
The players looked at his completely unharmed figure, and the hearts that had been hanging in suspense finally settled back down.
"We... won."
"What an unimaginable bitter battle."
One player sighed with emotion.
"It still had to be our boss. I believe Guild Leader Faustus will lead us to victory forever!"
A player clenched his fists tightly, his eyes filled with reverence.
"Of course. Just look at who God Faustus is. He’s a living legend!"
"Hahahaha, I’m so damn glad I didn’t join some other guild back then..."
"Master."
When Camille saw Daniel, she smiled and said, "That battle of yours truly left me in awe!"
"In the end, I only borrowed Oracle-grade Strength."
Daniel shook his head.
"Next, I have to participate in the Starlight Rankings, so I must continue improving my strength."
He told Camille about Golden Mountain’s invitation.
"To survive in the starry sky is to live by the law of the jungle."
Camille sighed.
"Even the ranking battles within a single starfield are already incomparably intense, let alone facing powerhouses from other domains."

"The hatred accumulated between the major starfields over countless years has long since seeped into their bones. Once they encounter participants from foreign domains, they will never show mercy. Master, you truly do need to take another step forward—make your sword even faster!"
"Mm."
Daniel nodded.
A few days later.
Earth Origin Core.
[Ding! You have successfully absorbed Earth Origin! Congratulations, you have completely taken control of Earth Origin and obtained the highest authority over Earth!]
[Ding! You have obtained [Origin Essence] ×100!]
[Notice: You may operate Earth’s management program through the world interface and unlock various functions.]
After Daniel finished absorbing the Origin, the system notification rang in his ears.
Origin Essence?
He looked at the system details.
[Origin Essence (???)]
Grade: ???
Effect: Can be used to unlock various world functions.
Special: Origin Essence is one of the top-tier materials used to construct a Divine Domain.
Description:

At the beginning of the universe, Origin power scattered across the void like countless stars. They nurtured, evolved, and ultimately transformed into innumerable vibrant worlds of life. Origin is the beginning of all living beings, the most primitive and purest form of the power of creation. It lies hidden in the depths of worlds, flowing through the folds of time, possessing endless and indescribable wondrous uses...
"Origin Essence... a top-tier divine material for constructing a Divine Domain!"
A sharp gleam flashed through Daniel’s eyes.
Once he broke through the shackles of level 400, he would have to begin condensing his own Divine Domain.
And if he wanted to forge a Divine Domain powerful enough to crush everything, then naturally, the foundation he used had to be as supreme as possible.
The Origin Essence currently in his possession was the most perfect choice he had selected from countless possibilities!
Thinking of this, he immediately tried to see whether it could be sold.
The result filled him with joy. This Origin Essence could actually be sold!
[Ding! You have sold [Origin Essence] ×100 to Doom Guild. Sale price: 1 copper coin. Millionfold Boost triggered!]
[The item sold is a special substance. Please choose quality boost / quantity boost!]
"Quantity boost!"
Daniel did not hesitate.
A mere hundred units was far too little. It was completely insufficient!
[Congratulations, you have obtained 1 gold coin! You have obtained [Origin Essence] ×100,000,000!]
Daniel looked at the one hundred million units of Origin Essence that had just arrived, and his eyes instantly lit up!
Just then—
[Ding! You have received a class change task.]
[Notice: A new task has been added to your task list. Please check it.]
Daniel opened the task list.
[Earth Origin Access Unlocked]
Forbidden-grade archer class change task
Restriction: Lord of Earth
Task Difficulty: epic-grade
Task Objective: Unlock all foundational systems of Earth Origin Access Unlocked, using Aetheria as the template.
Foundational systems include but are not limited to:
[Player Respawn System]
After access is unlocked, players who die on Earth may respawn.
[World Growth System]
After being unlocked, Earth may use world-growth items to upgrade.

Task Introduction: Unlocking the foundational systems of Earth Origin Access Unlocked requires a large amount of Origin Essence. If there is insufficient Origin Essence, Origin power will automatically overflow and condense. The time required depends on the strength of the living beings on the plane. Please check the world interface for specific details.
Task Duration: Long-term
Task Reward: [forbidden-grade archer Class Awakening Scroll (Level 360)] ×1.
Daniel read through the task details from beginning to end. Then, following the system’s prompt, he opened the world management interface.
Sure enough, the interface was filled with a long list of greyed-out functions that had not yet been unlocked.
He counted them. Unlocking everything would require a total of 100,000 Origin Essence.
If he followed the normal process and slowly accumulated it step by step, who knew how long he would have to wait?
"This is clearly a pit dug specifically for me to jump into—just like when I was level 80 and was forced to fight the World War to obtain world essence."
The corner of Daniel’s mouth twitched, revealing an "I knew it" smile.
"A standard trap!"
He sneered.
With the system backing him up and one hundred million units of Origin Essence in his hands, how could he possibly be stupid enough to wait for it to slowly increase on its own?
"Unlock everything right now!"
Without even blinking, he directly threw in 100,000 Origin Essence.
This bit of consumption could not even be considered a drop in the bucket.
[Ding! All options have been successfully unlocked.]

[Ding! You have successfully unlocked all foundational systems of Earth. A world announcement will now be issued, covering all territories under your name—Aetheria, Aerial Realm, Divine Wind Realm, Earth...]

[World Announcement: Player [Faustus] has successfully unlocked Earth’s foundational systems! All players, please take note—from now on, players may respawn after dying on Earth. At the same time, Earth will soon refresh a large number of wild monsters!]
A satisfied curve appeared at the corner of Daniel’s mouth.
[Ding! You have completed the class change task [Earth Origin Access Unlocked]!]
[Ding! You have obtained [forbidden-grade archer Class Awakening Scroll (Level 360)] ×1!]
This speed was practically like flying!
Daniel immediately pushed his level all the way to 360!
The moment he finished leveling up, a new class change task surged in like a tide.
[Earth Pioneer]
Forbidden-grade archer class change task
Restriction: Lord of Earth
Task Difficulty: epic-grade
Task Objectives:
Build at least seven main city-level cities on Earth.
Build a total of no fewer than one hundred towns and cities of various levels.
Task Introduction: Build Earth into the most solid rear fortress of the human race...
Task Duration: Long-term
Task Rewards: [forbidden-grade archer Class Awakening Scroll (Level 380)] ×1, [forbidden-grade archer Class Awakening Scroll (Level 400)] ×1.
Daniel was stunned for a moment.

chapters.title: Chapter 252 -252-Chaos Samsara Divine Domain
paragraphs: Two Class Awakening Scrolls from a single quest reward?
What was going on?
Still, he could not be bothered to dwell on it. If the system dared to give it, then he dared to take it.
The quest itself, however...
"Why do I feel like every single one of these quests is finding a new way to hold me back?"
Daniel felt a little annoyed. "Two quests in a row, and both of them want me to obediently stay at home, farm resources, and develop."
Don’t be fooled by the fact that he had completed the Earth Origin Access Unlocked quest in the blink of an eye. That was only because he had the Millionfold Boost system.
If he had followed the proper process step by step, this quest probably would have taken at least a year to complete!
"Good thing I chose the path of arcane technology back then."
Daniel shook his head in relief. "Only Arcane Machinery can get this pile of nonsense done as quickly as possible."
Without wasting another word, he immediately sent his puppet clones to coordinate and dispatch resources across the various planes.
Very soon, countless Arcane Machinery components and city modules were transported through the newly built Starfield Portals, pouring in from every direction in an endless stream.
Large numbers of guild players also swarmed over, each one full of energy and enthusiasm.

With everyone working together, it only took three days for seven magnificent main cities on the scale of starfield fortresses, along with one hundred large and small arcane-energy towns, to rise from the ground in perfect formation.
[Ding! You have completed the class change quest Earth Pioneer!]
[Ding! You have obtained forbidden-grade archer Class Awakening Scroll (Level 380) ×1, forbidden-grade archer Class Awakening Scroll (Level 400) ×1!]
Level 400!
He was only one final step away from crossing the threshold into supreme-grade.
After that, he could open up his Divine Domain and officially become a supreme-grade powerhouse.
The quest might have been a little infuriating, but there was absolutely nothing to complain about when it came to the reward!
Daniel did not hesitate in the slightest and quickly pushed his level upward.
[Ding! Congratulations, you have reached Level 400!]
[Notice: You have obtained the unique special achievement Level 400!]
[Ding! Achievement reward obtained: Divine Domain Secret Art (supreme-grade)!]
Daniel immediately traded away the reward.
[Ding! You have sold Divine Domain Secret Art (supreme-grade) to Doom Guild for 1 copper coin. Millionfold Boost triggered!]
[The sold item is categorized as a skill book. Please select: quality boost / quantity boost!]
"Quality boost!"

[Congratulations, you have obtained 1 gold coin! You have obtained the Divine-grade secret art Divine Domain Codex (Divine-grade) ×1! As the shackles of the world level shatter, the might of this skill will also break free from its restraints and climb to an even higher level.]
[Notice: The Divine Domain Codex can assist you in constructing a Perfect Divine Domain!]

[Notice: The forbidden-grade archer class change quest system has now completely ended. From this point onward, your level will be restricted by your Rank. Only by breaking through to a higher Rank can your strength continue to rise.]
As Daniel listened to the system notifications ringing out one after another, he froze where he stood.
A new rule had appeared.
From this day onward, class change quests had become a thing of the past.
In the future, as long as he broke through his Rank, he would be able to break through his level limit.
"Of course, the most important thing right now is that I can finally construct my Divine Domain and become supreme-grade!"
He had not forgotten about Endless Divine Power and Holy Condensation.
Once he learned those two secret arts, he would be able to kill sages above his level!
When that time came... hmph!
A trace of anticipation appeared on Daniel’s face.
"Divinity."
Camille spoke slowly, his voice low and solemn.

"In the depths of every living soul lies a spark of consciousness. The fiercer that flame burns, the closer one draws to the realm of gods. The reason living beings are living beings is precisely because they are born with spirituality."
"Divinity?"
Daniel listened intently, his gaze focused. "So a creature whose soul is powerful enough can be considered legendary-grade?"
"Exactly, my Master."
Camille nodded slightly. "Divinity is the foundation of immortality. That undying flame of Divinity is the most distinct mark of legendary-grade."

"However, relying solely on an undying flame is still not enough to step into the halls of supreme-grade. If a deity wishes to break through to supreme-grade, they must also condense a certain kind of ’Momentum.’"
Daniel nodded thoughtfully.
He had already reached the threshold of Level 400, yet he remained stuck outside the gate of supreme-grade.
He only knew that supreme-grade powerhouses all possessed a Divine Domain, but he did not know what a Divine Domain truly was.
Camille, however, was a peak demi-sage rank powerhouse. His understanding of Divine Domains was naturally far beyond Daniel’s.

Camille was not like him, someone who relied on experience points to rocket upward in level. Instead, he had advanced one step at a time, tempering his Mental State and breaking through bottlenecks across the long passage of years before finally reaching where he was today.
Those hardships had long since been carved into his bones. Because of that, every word he spoke carried weight.
"Momentum is the force born from the convergence of many powers."

Camille explained patiently, "Divinity and spirit are both bestowed by Heaven, yet they are separated from birth. Only by reforging the two into one can this ’Momentum’ be condensed. Once Momentum forms, the Domain is born."
He smiled faintly. "The next step is to construct the Divine Domain."
"So that’s how it is."
Daniel suddenly understood.
Now that he could no longer rely on class change quests to raise his level, it meant that he was no different from native beings like Camille.
He had to rely on the accumulation of Mental State and the breakthrough of Rank in order to continue climbing upward.
All the shortcuts he had once relied on had now transformed into layers of barriers.
His path of breakthrough was even harder than Camille’s, because he had almost no accumulation of Mental State at all. His foundation was as thin as a blank sheet of paper.
"But... I can still fleece the system one more time."
A smile tugged at the corner of Daniel’s mouth.
He still had a large number of Mental State points in his possession. He decided to pour all of them in.
[Ding! Mental State points can compensate for the Mental State you lack and fill the gaps in your Rank foundation. Would you like to use them?]
Daniel’s thoughts stirred.
So Mental State points were not used to "improve" his Mental State. They were used to "fill in what was missing"!
Without hesitation, he chose yes.
[Notice: You have consumed Mental State points. Your foundation of Divinity has been strengthened.]
[Notice: You have consumed Mental State points. You have comprehended Momentum.]
[Notice: You have consumed Mental State points. You have comprehended Divine Domain.]
[Ding! Please construct your Divine Domain immediately.]
When the last of his Mental State points was exhausted, Daniel had finally arrived before the threshold of constructing his Divine Domain.
He took out that achievement reward.
[Divine Domain Codex (Unique) (Divine-grade)]
Restriction: Faustus
Effect: After use, you may choose one from among numerous top-tier Divine Domain frameworks.

Description: Constructing a Divine Domain is the necessary path toward sage rank, as well as the foundation of sage rank. The more exceptional the framework you choose, the more unshakable your foundation will become, and the more terrifying the Strength you unleash after advancing to sage rank will be.
Daniel held the codex in his palm and took a deep breath.
A treasure like this was practically fate’s favor.
He thought to himself, "This thing is worth no less than my Crusader’s Physique."
Without hesitation, he opened it.
[Ding! You have used the Divine Domain Codex.]
In an instant, countless dazzling patterns of light unfolded before Daniel’s eyes.
They were all Divine Domain frameworks, and every single one could be considered top-tier.
He examined them one by one. In the end, he chose the pattern that resonated most closely with his soul!
[Notice: You have selected Chaos Samsara Realm!]
[Chaos Samsara Realm (Divine Domain Framework)]
Restriction: Faustus
Effect: Use the Immortal Singularity as the catalyst to resonate with the void, condense the Eyes of Divinity, and forge your own Divine Domain.
Special: To construct this Divine Domain, you must gather three types of Holy Relics — Divine Resonance, Divinity, and Divine Foundation.

Description: Chaos Samsara Realm — the living sink into endless reincarnation, while the dead fall into an eternal abyss. Life and destruction are decided within a single glance. This is a supreme realm that none may touch unless they are chosen by destiny.
"Chaos Samsara Realm..."
Daniel murmured softly.
The Divine Domain framework he had chosen would use the Immortal Singularity to condense two eyes of Divinity.
The left eye represented life.
The right eye represented death.
Life could cause enemies to sink into eternal intoxication and endless downfall.
Death could shatter an enemy’s Divine Soul, forcing them into self-destruction.
This was the power of samsara.
"Overwhelmingly powerful."
He clenched his fist and said in a low voice, "This is the one."
[Ding! You have obtained Chaos Samsara Realm. Please gather the required Holy Relics as soon as possible and complete the construction of your Divine Domain.]

Would you like to use them?]
Daniel’s thoughts stirred.
So Mental State points were not used to "improve" his Mental State.
They were used to "fill in what was missing"!
Without hesitation, he chose yes.
[Notice: You have consumed Mental State points.
Your foundation of Divinity has been strengthened.]
[Notice: You have consumed Mental State points.
You have comprehended Momentum.]
[Notice: You have consumed Mental State points.
You have comprehended Divine Domain.]
[Ding!
Please construct your Divine Domain immediately.]
When the last of his Mental State points was exhausted, Daniel had finally arrived before the threshold of constructing his Divine Domain.
He took out that achievement reward.
[Divine Domain Codex (Unique) (Divine-grade)]
Restriction: Faustus
Effect: After use, you may choose one from among numerous top-tier Divine Domain frameworks.
Description: Constructing a Divine Domain is the necessary path toward sage rank, as well as the foundation of sage rank.
The more exceptional the framework you choose, the more unshakable your foundation will become, and the more terrifying the Strength you unleash after advancing to sage rank will be.
Daniel held the codex in his palm and took a deep breath.
A treasure like this was practically fate’s favor.
He thought to himself, "This thing is worth no less than my Crusader’s Physique."
Without hesitation, he opened it.
[Ding!
You have used the Divine Domain Codex.]
In an instant, countless dazzling patterns of light unfolded before Daniel’s eyes.
They were all Divine Domain frameworks, and every single one could be considered top-tier.
He examined them one by one.
In the end, he chose the pattern that resonated most closely with his soul!
[Notice: You have selected Chaos Samsara Realm!]
[Chaos Samsara Realm (Divine Domain Framework)]
Restriction: Faustus
Effect: Use the Immortal Singularity as the catalyst to resonate with the void, condense the Eyes of Divinity, and forge your own Divine Domain.
Special: To construct this Divine Domain, you must gather three types of Holy Relics — Divine Resonance, Divinity, and Divine Foundation.
Description: Chaos Samsara Realm — the living sink into endless reincarnation, while the dead fall into an eternal abyss.
Life and destruction are decided within a single glance.
This is a supreme realm that none may touch unless they are chosen by destiny.
"Chaos Samsara Realm..."
Daniel murmured softly.
The Divine Domain framework he had chosen would use the Immortal Singularity to condense two eyes of Divinity.
The left eye represented life.
The right eye represented death.
Life could cause enemies to sink into eternal intoxication and endless downfall.
Death could shatter an enemy’s Divine Soul, forcing them into self-destruction.
This was the power of samsara.
"Overwhelmingly powerful."
He clenched his fist and said in a low voice, "This is the one."
[Ding!
You have obtained Chaos Samsara Realm.
Please gather the required Holy Relics as soon as possible and complete the construction of your Divine Domain.]

chapters.title: Chapter 253 -253-Studying Two Divine-grade Secret Arts
paragraphs: Boom—!
Daniel’s body trembled as he unfolded his Divine Domain.
In the void, a pair of eyes abruptly opened.
The left eye was as black as an abyss.
The right eye was as white as bone.
The left eye gazed upon death.
The right eye embraced life.
However, those eyes were empty and lifeless, without the slightest trace of spirituality. The domain they enveloped was nothing more than an illusory phantom.
"Sealing Crystal."
Daniel took out the bead that Justin had given him.
Before absorbing the Earth Origin, he had already completely sealed and refined the Angel King.
What had replaced it was the mysterious liquid now brimming inside the bead.
That liquid contained not only immortal Divinity, but also the unique holy aura of a Divine-grade powerhouse!
This was the highest quality Divinity!
Daniel tossed the Sealing Crystal into his Divine Domain.
With a soft pop, the bead shattered. The liquid inside poured out like a breached dam and was instantly absorbed by the pair of samsara eyes.
Buzz, buzz—!
The samsara eyes suddenly trembled, and a mighty pressure no weaker than a peak demi-sage rank erupted from them.
"And there’s still Origin Essence."
He poured all the remaining Origin Essence into it.
[Notice: You have used Origin Essence.]
The originally hollow and lifeless samsara eyes gradually became vivid after absorbing a vast amount of Origin Essence, as if something were slowly awakening deep within their pupils.
Daniel even had an illusion.
These eyes were about to give birth to their own will!
As Divine Resonance, the Origin Essence was also the finest of the finest.
"This is ridiculous."
Daniel was overjoyed.
Sensing that the might of his Divine Domain was already no weaker than that of a demi-sage, he nodded in satisfaction.
"I’m only missing the final Holy Relic now."
Constructing a Divine Domain required three things: Divine Resonance, Divinity, and Divine Foundation.
Ordinary supreme-grade powerhouses naturally did not require such top-tier materials. They could make do with whatever they found, which was precisely why they would remain mediocre.

From the very beginning, Daniel had chosen the top-tier Chaos Samsara Realm, which meant he was destined to walk a supreme path that would crush all living beings beneath him. That was why he had used the Sealing Crystal and Origin Essence as his foundation.
Of course, he could not compromise when it came to Divine Foundation either.
He simply had no interest in ordinary goods.
"Forget it. I’ll fill in the last part once I find a better Holy Relic in the future."
Some things could only be found by fortune, not by force.
He did not want to shortchange himself, so he decided to wait and see whether he could obtain the finest Divine Foundation later.
"For now, I can finally study Endless Divine Power and Holy Condensation!"
Now that his Divine Domain had taken shape, he finally had the qualifications to study the two secret arts from Luna_Fox.
[Ding! You have learned the secret art Endless Divine Power!]
He opened the details of the secret art.
[Endless Divine Power]
Restriction: supreme-grade
Grade: Divine-grade

Effect: Uses the Immortal Singularity to condense an invisible force that silently seeps into every cell of the target’s body, remaining dormant without erupting. The more times it is stacked, the more terrifying the accumulated damage becomes. This force is entirely under your control and may be triggered at any time.

Description: Every cell of a Divine-grade powerhouse has already transcended the mortal realm and entered the sacred. Ordinary blades, swords, and magic are extremely difficult to use to inflict fatal damage upon them. Only secret arts specifically designed to target a Divine-grade Constitution can be effective. Endless Divine Power is the pinnacle of such secret arts. It was created by an Oracle-grade of Luna_Fox, with the purpose of dismantling a sage’s body from its very foundation and delivering a fatal blow.
After Daniel finished reading, everything suddenly became clear to him.
"No wonder my damage felt like nothing more than a scratch when it landed on Divine-grade powerhouses. Their physical structure has already become completely different."
"If every single cell has transcended the mortal realm and entered the sacred, then that really isn’t something a legendary-grade can deal with."
The corner of his mouth lifted slightly.
"Now that I have Endless Divine Power, I can break through that turtle shell around Divine-grade powerhouses too."
This secret art was like a universal key made specifically for picking locks.
"As for the other secret art, it’s used to deal with the sage rank of Divine-grade sages."
Daniel learned Holy Condensation as well.
[Ding! You have studied the secret art Holy Condensation!]
[Holy Condensation]
Restriction: supreme-grade
Grade: Divine-grade

Effect: Continuously tempers the Divine Domain, pushing its toughness and power to the limit until it is comparable to low-grade sage rank. This secret art is divided into three stages. The first stage expands the foundation of the Divine Domain. The second stage strengthens the structure of the Divine Domain. The third stage tempers the essence of the Divine Domain.

Description: A sage’s sage rank can connect with the power of the world. To oppose sage rank is equivalent to opposing an entire world. Holy Condensation, however, walks the path of breaking all laws through sheer force. By tempering the Divine Domain to the extreme, one can directly contend against sage rank. This art also originated from Luna_Fox and was designed to forge the resilience and killing power of the Divine Domain.
"In other words, the limits of a Divine Domain really can contend head-on against sage rank."
Daniel secretly marveled.
As expected of Divine-grade secret arts. They were truly hidden inheritances that ordinary powerhouses would never have the chance to witness.
From this alone, one could see just how powerful Luna_Fox was!
Two secret arts this heaven-defying were actually part of their foundation.
"So this is what true heritage looks like."
He sighed with emotion.
"I’ll start studying it now."
Holy Condensation was divided into three stages. He had to start from the first stage and build upward step by step.
Canaan Starfield, Misty Rain Galaxy.
Luna_Fox Star System.
"Gorby, it has been a long time."
The instructor in hemp robes greeted an Oracle-grade with a smile. However, his gaze landed on the white-robed young man standing beside Gorby.
"This must be your student, James, yes? He truly is extraordinary!"
Then he pointed at the black-clothed young man beside him and said with a smile,
"This is my student, Mosi."
Oracle-grade Gorby looked Mosi up and down a few times.
"I heard that the top position on the Luna_Fox Golden Ranking has been occupied by Mosi for over a hundred years. I imagine his strength must be exceptional."
"I brought my student all the way from Frostfall Galaxy precisely because we wanted to experience it for ourselves!"
"My old friend, you must give us a fair arrangement."
"My student is already prepared as well."
James smiled faintly, his voice clear and confident.
"Please enlighten me."
The instructor in hemp robes nodded with a smile.
"Then please rest for a moment, both of you. I will arrange the venue right away."
He turned and left with Mosi.
"Mosi, do you understand what this battle means for you?"
The instructor suddenly asked.
"I understand."
Mosi was a man of few words.
"If I lose, it’s almost certain death."
"That’s right."
The instructor in hemp robes sighed. "To be honest, I originally didn’t want you to fight. But aside from you, I’m afraid no one in Luna_Fox can stop James."
"It doesn’t matter."
A trace of battle intent ignited in Mosi’s eyes.
"This matter is not entirely bad either."
The instructor explained, "James has been challenging others everywhere for the sake of condensing an ’Invincible Momentum.’"

"Once that Momentum is formed, after he breaks through to Divine-grade, he will immediately stand at the peak of Divine-grade. But if you can defeat him at this moment, then all the Momentum he worked so hard to accumulate before this will transfer to you."
"I understand."
Mosi nodded.
"That is why you absolutely must win."
The instructor’s tone grew heavy.
If Mosi won this battle, then James would be making a wedding dress for him.
But if he lost...
James was someone who had swept through the entire Frostfall Galaxy without a single opponent!
Do not be fooled by his gentle appearance. Deep down, he was extremely ruthless.
Rumor had it that ninety percent of the powerhouses who lost to him had died on the spot, while the remaining ten percent had been crippled.
Either he did not strike at all, or once he struck, he struck to kill.
But this was normal.
In a true life-and-death battle, one could only comprehend the true meaning of life on the edge of death. Only in absolute desperation could one unleash all of their potential.
This was also why these peerless geniuses all needed guardians by their side.

You might have the time of your life fighting, but if you killed a genius that another faction had poured countless resources and effort into nurturing, would they not come after you with their lives on the line?
Mosi was the instructor’s proudest student, as well as the strongest fighter among Luna_Fox’s younger generation.

If Luna_Fox casually sent out a second-rate student and allowed James to crush them in just a few moves, wouldn’t that be the same as announcing to the entire world that Luna_Fox had declined and could no longer produce even a single decent junior?
Therefore, Mosi had no path of retreat.
But the reward was just as tempting.
One step to the heavens.
Everything depended on this battle!
"James."
Gorby looked at his proudest student.
"How confident are you?"
James pondered for a moment. His tone was cautious, like that of an old schemer calculating his next move.
"Teacher, this student believes... I have approximately a ninety-nine percent chance of victory."
"Approximately."
"Ninety-nine percent."
When these two phrases were combined, they sounded especially intriguing.
"Ninety-nine percent?"
The corner of Gorby’s mouth twitched.
This student of his was good in every way, except that he was far too "modest."
"You’re still not good enough at pretending."
Gorby cursed inwardly, though his expression remained calm on the surface.
"End it quickly. There is still another force in Misty Rain Galaxy waiting for us to visit. After this match is over, we’ll head straight to the next one."
"No problem, Teacher."
James lowered his head respectfully.
This time, Luna_Fox had specifically opened up a secret realm for the challenge match.
Oracle-grade powerhouses had the ability to independently open small secret realms. The higher their Rank, the more stable and realistic the secret realms they created would be.
The past Oracle-grades of Luna_Fox had left behind countless such secret realms. They could simply pick one at random and use it.
After all, even if it was destroyed, no one would feel sorry for it.

chapters.title: Chapter 254 -254-The Top-Tier Divine Heir Is a Piece of Trash
paragraphs: Outside the secret realm.
"James, do you have anything else to say before you go?"
Gorby looked at his student, his tone carrying a hint of kindness.
James blinked confidently, the corner of his mouth lifting slightly.
"Teacher... after this fight is over, don’t forget to hand out the reward."
"You little brat!"
Gorby laughed and cursed, but the affection in his eyes could not be hidden.
"At this rate, my entire fortune will be emptied out by you sooner or later."
"How can you call that ’emptying you out’?"
James refuted him with a perfectly serious expression. "A teacher rewarding his student is only right and proper!"
Gorby rolled his eyes, too lazy to argue with him.
On the other side.
"Mosi, are you ready?"
The instructor in hemp robes looked at his student with concern and asked in a low voice, "How confident are you?"
Mosi fell silent for a moment before slowly spitting out a few words.
"About fifty percent."
"Pretend I never asked."
The instructor in hemp robes smiled awkwardly.
No matter what Mosi did, whenever someone asked about his odds, his answer was always half.
Yet every single time, he would crush his opponents with overwhelming force.
So what was the difference between asking and not asking?
"Fight well."
"Okay."
Mosi was a man of few words, as cold as a block of stone.
It was as if saying even one more word would cost him his life.
But at that very moment!
A vast spatial fluctuation descended without warning, so oppressive that it nearly made everyone unable to breathe.
The expressions of the instructor in hemp robes and Gorby changed at the same time.
A high Oracle-grade.
At least T6!
"A T6 Oracle-grade powerhouse!"
The instructor’s heart trembled.
He himself was only Tier 4. In Luna_Fox, he was already considered a ranked expert, but compared to the newcomer, the gap was far from small.
"Who is it?"
Gorby, however, was a little more curious.
Although he was also Tier 4, he had a T7 Oracle-grade backing him, so he naturally had much more confidence.
Buzz, buzz—!
Space seemed to be torn open from the center by an invisible hand, splitting into a smooth rift.
A powerhouse slowly stepped out from within.
He wore a black robe, and the hem of that robe was embroidered with an incomparably dazzling golden mountain — the emblem of the strongest force in Canaan Starfield.
Golden Mountain’s T6 Oracle-grade — Angel.
"Greetings, envoy of Golden Mountain!"
The instructor in hemp robes hurriedly bowed.
"Greetings, envoy."
Gorby also bent forward.
"Greetings, envoy of Golden Mountain."
James and Mosi saluted at the same time.
Angel smiled and raised his hand slightly, his voice gentle.
"No need for formalities. We are all old acquaintances. There is no need to be so restrained."
Both Frostfall Galaxy and Misty Rain Galaxy belonged to Canaan Starfield, and Golden Mountain was the true overlord of this starfield.
Naturally, the Oracle-grades present all recognized this renowned Angel.
"I imagine you have already guessed a little about why I came this time."
Two invitations glowing with golden light appeared out of thin air in Angel’s hand as he smiled.

"This Starlight Rankings Tournament is completely different from the previous ones. James and Mosi must both participate. Your match ends here. Go back and prepare properly. Then go meet the geniuses from the other starfields together."
The instructor in hemp robes and Gorby exchanged glances, then each revealed a helpless smile.
"Well then... looks like this fight won’t be happening."
James and Mosi, however, remained calm.
"Who I fight makes no difference."
Mosi’s face was expressionless, his voice as cold as iron.
"Fighting geniuses from other starfields?"
James’s eyes suddenly lit up, as if he had seen countless glittering gold coins.
He had to use this chance to properly fleece his teacher and Golden Mountain!
God Realm.
A deep spatial passage had already opened.
One end was connected to the towering halls of the God Realm, while the other pointed toward distant Aetheria!
Four legendary-grade Godkin powerhouses were waiting restlessly at the entrance of the passage, each of their expressions uglier than the last.
"Why isn’t Simon here yet? Time is almost up!"
A bearded Godkin man stomped his foot hard, anger suppressed in his voice.
"If we miss this opportunity, the spatial passage will close, and the mission to destroy Aetheria will be completely ruined."
A golden-curled Godkin had a gloomy expression.
"The consequences of mission failure — who can afford to bear them?"
"That damned useless trash. Absolutely hateful!"
A broad and burly Godkin spat fiercely.
"No wonder he’s the son of the Pantheon Summit Hall’s hall master, yet has fallen so low that he has to mix with people like us."
"Enough, enough. Simon is still a descendant of the hall master, after all. What’s wrong with him arriving a little late?"
A Godkin with a scar across his face spoke slowly.

"The Pantheon Summit Hall stands above the temples of the gods. Its status is right there. If those words you just said reach his ears, be careful he doesn’t settle accounts with each of you in the future."
"Him?"
The blond Godkin sneered, his face full of disdain.
"It’s still a question whether that piece of trash can ever return to Pantheon Summit Hall. And you think he can make a comeback?"
"Exactly. Simon was born with weak Divinity. After so many years, he’s still nothing more than a mere legendary-grade. What’s the difference between him and trash?"
"If I had his family background, I would have become a demi-sage long ago."
"A piece of trash wants to turn things around? Hilarious!"
The Godkin powerhouses mocked him one after another, their words full of ridicule.
In their eyes, Simon, who had noble birth but was born defective, was nothing more than a joke to laugh about over tea.
Simon flew toward the gathering point at an unhurried pace.
When those so-called "companions" saw him, their eyes were filled with undisguised contempt.
"Look, the God Realm’s number one piece of trash is here."
"That’s him. The son of the Pantheon Summit Hall’s hall master — Trash Simon."
"Shh — don’t let him hear you."
"What are you afraid of? I’m a supreme-grade, and he’s just a god-grade. So what if he hears me?"
Simon’s face remained expressionless, as if he had heard nothing at all, and he continued flying forward.
Yet in his mind, memories from one hundred thousand years ago surged like a rusted knife, carving into his heart again and again.
One hundred thousand years ago.
There was a human powerhouse named Kelly who set foot in the God Realm and entered that forbidden land that even sages paled at the mention of — the Bloodtide Sea.
"Bloodtide Sea..."
The moment Simon thought of that name, his entire body trembled uncontrollably, and a deep fear flashed through his eyes.
Legend had it that in the deepest part of the Bloodtide Sea, there was a "Gate of Truth." By passing through it, one could arrive at another universe at random.
But the price was so great that even Divine-grade powerhouses could not endure it.
Back then, Simon had been a guard of the Bloodtide Sea.
"I was still very weak then. Father God looked down on me. My younger brothers looked down on me. The entire God Realm looked down on me."

"Those younger brothers of mine were terrified that if I remained in Pantheon Summit Hall, I would be an eyesore to them and compete with them for resources. So they joined forces and drove me to the Bloodtide Sea."
The Bloodtide Sea.
The number one forbidden land of the God Realm!
Even Divine-grade powerhouses had a nine-in-ten chance of dying if they entered. Only living beings with unwavering beliefs and wills as firm as steel could survive there.
It was there that Simon first met a human from Aetheria.
It was also the first time he witnessed a kind of Strength he had never seen before.
It was not some extraordinary talent.
It was not some Bloodline Inheritance.
It was belief and will carved deep into the bones.
And the one he could never forget for all eternity was Kelly.
In his long and cold life, Kelly was the only person who had never once looked at him as if he were trash!

sentences.text: Outside the secret realm.
"James, do you have anything else to say before you go?"
Gorby looked at his student, his tone carrying a hint of kindness.
James blinked confidently, the corner of his mouth lifting slightly.
"Teacher... after this fight is over, don’t forget to hand out the reward."
"You little brat!"
Gorby laughed and cursed, but the affection in his eyes could not be hidden.
"At this rate, my entire fortune will be emptied out by you sooner or later."
"How can you call that ’emptying you out’?"
James refuted him with a perfectly serious expression.
"A teacher rewarding his student is only right and proper!"
Gorby rolled his eyes, too lazy to argue with him.
On the other side.
"Mosi, are you ready?"
The instructor in hemp robes looked at his student with concern and asked in a low voice, "How confident are you?"
Mosi fell silent for a moment before slowly spitting out a few words.
"About fifty percent."
"Pretend I never asked."
The instructor in hemp robes smiled awkwardly.
No matter what Mosi did, whenever someone asked about his odds, his answer was always half.
Yet every single time, he would crush his opponents with overwhelming force.
So what was the difference between asking and not asking?
"Fight well."
"Okay."
Mosi was a man of few words, as cold as a block of stone.
It was as if saying even one more word would cost him his life.
But at that very moment!
A vast spatial fluctuation descended without warning, so oppressive that it nearly made everyone unable to breathe.
The expressions of the instructor in hemp robes and Gorby changed at the same time.
A high Oracle-grade.
At least T6!
"A T6 Oracle-grade powerhouse!"
The instructor’s heart trembled.
He himself was only Tier 4.
In Luna_Fox, he was already considered a ranked expert, but compared to the newcomer, the gap was far from small.
"Who is it?"
Gorby, however, was a little more curious.
Although he was also Tier 4, he had a T7 Oracle-grade backing him, so he naturally had much more confidence.
Buzz, buzz—!
Space seemed to be torn open from the center by an invisible hand, splitting into a smooth rift.
A powerhouse slowly stepped out from within.
He wore a black robe, and the hem of that robe was embroidered with an incomparably dazzling golden mountain — the emblem of the strongest force in Canaan Starfield.
Golden Mountain’s T6 Oracle-grade — Angel.
"Greetings, envoy of Golden Mountain!"
The instructor in hemp robes hurriedly bowed.
"Greetings, envoy."
Gorby also bent forward.
"Greetings, envoy of Golden Mountain."
James and Mosi saluted at the same time.
Angel smiled and raised his hand slightly, his voice gentle.
"No need for formalities.
We are all old acquaintances.
There is no need to be so restrained."
Both Frostfall Galaxy and Misty Rain Galaxy belonged to Canaan Starfield, and Golden Mountain was the true overlord of this starfield.
Naturally, the Oracle-grades present all recognized this renowned Angel.
"I imagine you have already guessed a little about why I came this time."
Two invitations glowing with golden light appeared out of thin air in Angel’s hand as he smiled.
"This Starlight Rankings Tournament is completely different from the previous ones.
James and Mosi must both participate.
Your match ends here.
Go back and prepare properly.
Then go meet the geniuses from the other starfields together."
The instructor in hemp robes and Gorby exchanged glances, then each revealed a helpless smile.
"Well then... looks like this fight won’t be happening."
James and Mosi, however, remained calm.
"Who I fight makes no difference."
Mosi’s face was expressionless, his voice as cold as iron.
"Fighting geniuses from other starfields?"
James’s eyes suddenly lit up, as if he had seen countless glittering gold coins.
He had to use this chance to properly fleece his teacher and Golden Mountain!
God Realm.
A deep spatial passage had already opened.
One end was connected to the towering halls of the God Realm, while the other pointed toward distant Aetheria!
Four legendary-grade Godkin powerhouses were waiting restlessly at the entrance of the passage, each of their expressions uglier than the last.
"Why isn’t Simon here yet?
Time is almost up!"
A bearded Godkin man stomped his foot hard, anger suppressed in his voice.
"If we miss this opportunity, the spatial passage will close, and the mission to destroy Aetheria will be completely ruined."
A golden-curled Godkin had a gloomy expression.
"The consequences of mission failure — who can afford to bear them?"
"That damned useless trash.
Absolutely hateful!"
A broad and burly Godkin spat fiercely.
"No wonder he’s the son of the Pantheon Summit Hall’s hall master, yet has fallen so low that he has to mix with people like us."
"Enough, enough.
Simon is still a descendant of the hall master, after all.
What’s wrong with him arriving a little late?"
A Godkin with a scar across his face spoke slowly.
"The Pantheon Summit Hall stands above the temples of the gods.
Its status is right there.
If those words you just said reach his ears, be careful he doesn’t settle accounts with each of you in the future."
"Him?"
The blond Godkin sneered, his face full of disdain.
"It’s still a question whether that piece of trash can ever return to Pantheon Summit Hall.
And you think he can make a comeback?"
"Exactly.
Simon was born with weak Divinity.
After so many years, he’s still nothing more than a mere legendary-grade.
What’s the difference between him and trash?"
"If I had his family background, I would have become a demi-sage long ago."
"A piece of trash wants to turn things around?
Hilarious!"
The Godkin powerhouses mocked him one after another, their words full of ridicule.
In their eyes, Simon, who had noble birth but was born defective, was nothing more than a joke to laugh about over tea.
Simon flew toward the gathering point at an unhurried pace.
When those so-called "companions" saw him, their eyes were filled with undisguised contempt.
"Look, the God Realm’s number one piece of trash is here."
"That’s him.
The son of the Pantheon Summit Hall’s hall master — Trash Simon."
"Shh — don’t let him hear you."
"What are you afraid of?
I’m a supreme-grade, and he’s just a god-grade.
So what if he hears me?"
Simon’s face remained expressionless, as if he had heard nothing at all, and he continued flying forward.
Yet in his mind, memories from one hundred thousand years ago surged like a rusted knife, carving into his heart again and again.
One hundred thousand years ago.
There was a human powerhouse named Kelly who set foot in the God Realm and entered that forbidden land that even sages paled at the mention of — the Bloodtide Sea.

chapters.title: Chapter 255 -255-The Dark and Bloody Endless Starsea
paragraphs: "Kelly, every living being thinks I’m trash. Why are you... different?"
Simon had once asked her this out of curiosity.
Kelly smiled and asked in return, "Simon, just because everyone believes something is right, does that mean it must be right?"

"In my eyes, life is beautiful precisely because it comes in countless shapes and forms. Should every living being look the same, possess the same abilities, and hold the same opinions? Is that what people call good? I don’t think so."
Back then, Simon had only half understood her words.
All he knew was that he was happy. Very, very happy.
At long last, there was finally someone in this world who did not treat him as trash, but as a soul of flesh and blood, a soul with dignity.
Some time later, Kelly relied on her astonishing talent and willpower to break into the middle layer of the Bloodtide Sea.
Simon used his authority as a guard to find her.
When he saw that figure—tortured until she barely looked human, yet still gritting her teeth and refusing to fall—his heart felt as if something had seized it viciously.
"Kelly, give up."
He advised her out of kindness. "It’s too painful. You’ll never be able to reach the deepest part."
Kelly forced out a faint smile. She was a girl who loved to smile.
"Simon, how could you think that? We of the Aetheria human race have never believed in anything called ’impossible.’"
"We only believe in whether one has determination. As long as you have determination, you can definitely do it."
"Really?"
Simon blinked. He felt as if something inside his mind had cracked open, allowing a ray of light to seep in.
"Then... if I have determination, can I become the strongest in the God Realm too?"
"Of course, Simon," Kelly said with certainty.
"But I’m crippled, Kelly!" Simon said, both shocked and dejected.
"Simon, the flaw you were born with is only an obstacle at the starting line. It is not your destination."
Kelly smiled, and there was a conviction in that smile that made it impossible to refute.

"I’ve always felt that rather than chasing after something as vague and illusory as ’the strongest in the God Realm,’ it would be better to keep your feet on the ground and become the ’strongest Simon.’"
"You are you. You don’t need to live as someone else’s shadow. Compare yourself only to yourself. Surpass the person you were yesterday."
"Wouldn’t becoming the strongest Simon be far more meaningful than those empty titles?"
This time, Simon truly took her words to heart.
His eyes grew hot, and somewhere in his chest, it felt as if a fire had been lit, burning fiercely.
Toward Kelly, he developed a deep gratitude.
"Kelly... you’ll reach the deepest part of the Bloodtide Sea, right?"
he asked.
"I will, Simon. I will definitely reach that place."
Kelly’s voice was very soft, yet incomparably firm.
"Why do you have to reach that place?"
Simon did not understand.
Kelly’s smile suddenly faded, and a thin layer of sorrow surfaced in her eyes.
She sighed softly. "Because... I’ve already failed to keep a promise I made to someone. I don’t want to fail at the most important thing he entrusted to me as well."
"Right now, I can’t save my people. But I have to do something. Even if I have to risk this life of mine, I must find a way to save them."
Carrying that sense of impact within him, Simon returned to his post.
Many years later, relying on the belief he had drawn from Kelly, he tempered his physical body to an unimaginable degree.
With a single finger, he could crush a supreme-grade expert to death!
Although his mind power remained weak, forever stuck at the legendary-grade level, his true strength had become a secret known to no one.
"All of this is because of Kelly. Without her, there would be no Simon today."
He wanted to find her.
At long last, in the deepest part of the Bloodtide Sea, he saw Kelly again.
"Kelly, you would rather endure all these years here than push open that Door of Truth?"
Simon’s voice was full of confusion. "You clearly had the ability to push it open long ago..."
"Do you know what the price of opening that door is?"
Kelly asked weakly, her voice like a candle flame flickering in the wind.
"What is it?"
"It is... to forget everything."
The corners of Kelly’s lips curved upward.
It was as if she had seen a day from long, long ago...
That afternoon after the rain in Soul Devouring Vale. That figure descending from the sky. And the rainbow she had clutched tightly in her palm.
"If you refuse to forget, then why won’t you leave?"
Simon was even more confused. "Why are you staying here? What exactly is it for?"
Kelly’s smile did not change. She said faintly, "Perhaps... whether one lets go or stays behind, both require the same amount of courage."
"Simon, what is the Endless Starsea... like?"
she suddenly asked.
Simon fell silent for a long time, as if searching through his memories for an answer.
"I looked through a vast number of ancient records,"
he said in a low voice. "But when I reached the end of every book, only two words remained—cruelty."

"Those experts of the God Realm, those experts from other worlds, and even the ancient beings from millions of years ago—every single one of them said the same thing: the starry sky is cruel. The weak are prey to the strong. Blood flows like rivers!"
"Kelly, don’t push open that door. Even if you go through, you’ll only be leaping from one hell into another, even deeper hell."
Kelly continued to smile, the curve of her lips unchanged.
"Simon, just because everyone believes something is right, does that mean it must be right?"
she asked in return. "Are we only allowed to lower our heads and obediently endure everything fate forces upon us?"
"I think... what everyone believes to be right may not necessarily be right. I’ve always wanted to do something different, to give this world one more choice."
"Besides cruelty, there can still be another choice."
Kelly’s voice was very soft, yet every word carried weight.
"Then... will you push open that door?"
Simon’s voice tightened. "Your memories—are they more important to you than this belief?"
"There is someone who is very important to me."
Kelly’s gaze pierced through the void and landed upon that door, half real and half illusory. It was as if she were looking toward a place very, very far away.
"If you ever meet Faustus of the human race... tell him for me that Kelly is already dead."
"I don’t know whether I’ll push open that door. I don’t know how long I’ll remain here either..."
That was the last time Simon saw Kelly.
Kelly...
Are you still in the Bloodtide Sea now?
Simon shook his head, pressing those surging memories back into the depths of his heart.
Before his eyes, the spatial passage leading to Aetheria had already opened wide.
"I’m going to destroy your homeland, Kelly."
He said silently in his heart, "But you were right. The Endless Starsea should not have only one way to live."
"I’ve already found a way to notify the person you could never forget—Faustus."
"I’m sorry... I couldn’t lie to you."
Bitterness welled up in Simon’s heart. "I told him where you were as well."
"If... if you’re still alive, perhaps the two of you can meet again."
He took a deep breath and descended beside the four Godkin experts.
"Simon, why are you only arriving now?"
His teammate’s voice was filled with impatience.
Simon’s expression remained calm. He did not care about their thoughts at all.
Faustus silently sensed his Divine Domain.
He had already mastered the secret technique he had learned from Luna_Fox to its utmost limit.
Not long ago, he had still been only a legendary-grade archer.
Now, one of his feet had already stepped onto the threshold of a quasi-sage.
The speed at which his strength had risen was so fast that even he found it somewhat unreal. And yet, every single step had been incredibly stable.
"Only... I’m still missing one kind of Holy Relic."
he murmured. "My Divine Domain has yet to reach perfection. Although I can already contend with a sage rank expert right now, this still isn’t my strongest form."
"If I can obtain a supreme treasure capable of constructing my Divine Foundation and push my Divine Domain to perfection... that will be true invincibility."
Suddenly, Faustus’s mind stirred, and he abruptly raised his head.
In the void, space became like the surface of water wrinkled by the wind. Silent ripples spread outward in ring after ring.
"Someone’s here."
Camille’s pupils contracted sharply, and her hand was already resting on the hilt of her sword.
"Who could it be?"
Faustus raised an eyebrow.
Whoosh—!
A figure appeared without the slightest warning.
The newcomer wore luxurious robes, with a refined and dignified bearing. His strength was unfathomable.
Faustus and Camille both furrowed their brows instinctively...

chapters.title: Chapter 256 -256-The Gift from the Human Ancestor
paragraphs: "He’s human..."
Camille looked at Faustus, then at the newcomer, and most of the wariness in her heart faded away.
Faustus, however, looked puzzled.
Human?
There were countless branches of humanity throughout the Endless Starsea. Who knew which branch this person belonged to?
The human expert spread out his mind power, sensing the features and aura of this world.
"So this is the ancestral homeland spoken of in the legends of my human race..."
The expert withdrew his mind power, and his gaze slowly fell withdrew his mind power, and his gaze slowly fell upon Faustus.
He sized him up for a moment. Then, a sharp gleam suddenly flashed through his eyes.
"This young man... is anything but simple!"
He was secretly astonished. "Even among the rising talents my Chaos Humans have poured vast resources into nurturing, there probably aren’t many who can stand shoulder to shoulder with him."
There was shock in his expression, but also a trace of gratification.
The ancestral homeland had fallen silent for endless ages, yet it could still give birth to such an astonishingly brilliant prodigy. That was truly no easy feat.
A warm smile appeared on his face.
"My name is Hyman. I am of the Chaos Humans, a T6 Oracle-grade."
He glanced at Camille, then fixed his gaze steadily on Faustus and slowly asked,
"You... should be the one in charge here, correct?"
Hyman was a T6 Oracle-grade.
With his rank, he could suppress his own aura at will and avoid rejection by the rules of this small world.
With that sweep of mind power just now, he had seen through every living being in this world.
Only the human expert before him possessed quasi-sage combat strength. Unless something unexpected had happened, this person was the ruler of the ancestral homeland.
A T6 Oracle-grade!
Faustus understood very well what that meant.
He and Camille exchanged a silent glance, both of them shaken to the core.
"Faustus of the human race greets Your Excellency."
Faustus saluted neither servilely nor arrogantly, his voice clear and steady.
"Camille, a war general under Faustus’s command, greets Your Excellency."
Camille lowered her head and gave a respectful salute.
Faustus was no longer the ignorant, reckless youth he had once been.
He knew exactly what weight the title of T6 Oracle-grade carried.
Above sage was Oracle-grade.
Oracle-grade was divided into nine tiers. Tiers One through Three were low-grade, Tiers Four through Six were mid-grade, and Tiers Seven through Nine were high-grade.
Among them, T9 Oracle-grade basically only existed in ancient records. Everyone had heard of them, but no one had ever seen one.
Therefore, T8 Oracle-grade represented the peak combat power of the current Endless Starsea.
And even T8 Oracle-grade experts were as rare as phoenix feathers and qilin horns.
Under most circumstances, a T7 Oracle-grade was already enough to be the leader of a major faction.
A T6 Oracle-grade, meanwhile, was the backbone and main force of any great power, enjoying an incredibly exalted status.
Just like that emissary Angel from Gold-Grade Mountain. He alone had been enough to make countless factions lower their heads.
And now, the emissary sent by the Chaos Humans was actually also a T6 Oracle-grade!
Hyman nodded slightly, the corners of his lips lifting into a faint smile.
"Faustus... not a bad name."

"My Chaos Humans originally walked out from this ancestral homeland. Our ancestor has always been deeply concerned about this place, so he specially sent me here to make a trip and see with my own eyes what the ancestral homeland looks like now."

There was a hint of emotion in Hyman’s tone. "From what I see, divine power has begun to surge through this land once more. Given enough time, it will surely regain the resplendent glory it possessed in the ancient era."
Faustus and Camille remained silent. Neither of them replied.
"Faustus."
Hyman suddenly changed the topic. "Do you know where my Chaos Humans are now?"
"I do not."
Faustus shook his head.
"Hahaha..."
Hyman burst into laughter. "The Chaos Humans are currently in the Chaosverse, which neighbors the Myriad-Star Cosmos where you are now!"
Hiss—!
Faustus’s brows furrowed tightly.
A different universe!
"They’re actually... in another universe."
He murmured, looking somewhat dazed for a moment.
Seeing the stunned expression on this human junior’s face, Hyman immediately smiled.

"My human race once settled in the Myriad-Star Cosmos as well. Later, however, we formed a feud with a major power, so we traveled far away to the Chaosverse and forcefully carved out a foundation for ourselves there."
"A very, very long time ago, our entire race had already migrated over."
"So that’s how it is."
Faustus came to a realization.

The Chaos Humans had once survived in the Myriad-Star Cosmos as well. After falling out with some faction, they had simply sought another path in a different universe. Now, the entire race had taken root over there.
"So,"
Hyman looked at him meaningfully and said slowly, "in the end, this ancestral homeland must still be handed over to you to manage."
"The ancestor places great importance on this place. If you can develop this land properly, the ancestor will definitely not treat you unfairly."
"May I ask... what rank has the ancestor reached?"
Faustus suddenly asked.
"T8 Oracle-grade."
Hyman smiled faintly.
Buzz—!
It was as if a thunderclap exploded inside Faustus’s mind.
T8 Oracle-grade...
That was practically an existence standing at the very peak of this world.
If T9 Oracle-grade experts did not reveal themselves, then T8 was invincible.
The ancestor of the Chaos Humans was actually a T8 Oracle-grade. Truly terrifying beyond measure.
"According to the customs of my Chaos Humans, since this is our first meeting..."
Hyman extended his hand. In his palm, a palm-sized clump of soil appeared out of thin air.
"I should at least prepare a greeting gift for you."
"This is Chaos Black Soil. It is extremely rare, the kind of thing one can only encounter by chance and never seek by force."
He handed the treasure forward, his tone so casual that it was as if he were passing over a stone picked up by the roadside.
"This item can barely be considered presentable. From what I see, you seem to be in the process of constructing your Divine Domain. It should be useful to you. Take it."
Faustus’s eyes lit up. Especially when he heard that it would be extremely useful for constructing his Divine Domain, he quickly reached out and accepted it.
"I was just lacking a Divine Foundation for constructing my Divine Domain. I didn’t expect this surprise to come so suddenly."
"With this Chaos Black Soil, the Chaos Samsara Rank can truly reach perfection."
He held that unremarkable black clump of soil in his hand, but his heart was as clear as a mirror.
His own foundation had long since been seen through completely by this human expert.
But that made sense. For a T6 Oracle-grade to see through his true condition was as simple as drinking water.
Precisely because of that, Hyman had taken out the thing Faustus needed most at this moment.
As expected of a senior of the human race. This thoughtfulness was truly considerate.
Hyman naturally noticed Faustus’s excitement and nodded with a smile.
To ordinary people, this thing was indeed a priceless treasure that could only be encountered by chance.
But it also depended on who was looking at it.
In the eyes of a T6 Oracle-grade, the greatest value of this treasure probably did not lie in its use, but in its collectability.
"You are a swordsman?"
Hyman suddenly turned his head and looked at Camille.
Camille froze for a moment. After coming back to her senses, she hurriedly replied,
"Yes, Your Excellency. This junior has always walked with the sword as my companion."
"The path you’re taking is quite interesting."
A trace of appreciation flashed through Hyman’s eyes.
"Faintly, it even carries a bit of the shadow of the Sword God of my Chaos Humans."
He paused, then smiled and said, "What a coincidence. The path I mainly cultivate is also the Dao of the Sword. Today, I shall pass the sword arts of my Chaos Humans on to you."
"Thank you, Your Excellency!"
Camille’s entire body trembled, and even her voice quivered slightly.

The path she walked was completely different from the traditional paths to sainthood in the Myriad-Star Cosmos. She had explored it all by herself, feeling her way forward step by step, falling into countless pits and taking countless detours along the way.
Even now, despite already having the ability to attempt a breakthrough into divine-grade, she still did not dare to take that step.
She was afraid that once her path took shape, it would be too late to turn back in the future.
And Hyman was a T6 Oracle-grade who primarily cultivated the Dao of the Sword, an existence standing at the peak of the Endless Starsea.
To receive guidance from such a powerful expert was, to Camille, no less than a gift from fate itself.
This was not merely the passing down of teachings.
It was a smooth road leading straight toward the summit.

chapters.title: Chapter 257 -257-The Divine Domain Is Complete; Returning to the God Realm
paragraphs: "This sword Dao is called the Blade of Ruin."
Hyman waved his hand, sending a streak of flowing light into Camille’s forehead. His voice was clear and sharp, like the cry of a sword.

"When you can merge the three thousand sword strikes within the Blade of Ruin into a single sword strike, this sword Dao can be considered to have achieved minor success. At that time, once you step into divine-grade, you will be able to directly reach the peak of divine-grade."
"Thank you for your generous gift, Your Excellency!"
Camille bowed deeply, his voice trembling with irrepressible excitement.
This was not merely a sword art. It was a bridge built for him at the edge of a cliff.
In his own expectations, he might have remained stuck here for the rest of his life. Yet now, after this sudden turn of fortune, what lay before him was a broad road leading straight ahead!
"Hahaha."
Hyman stood with his hands behind his back and smiled faintly.
"Just assist Faustus well. Faustus of the human race, I hope to hear news of you soon."
"Farewell, Your Excellency."
Faustus saluted.
"Farewell, Your Excellency."
Camille bowed.
Whoosh—!
Hyman’s figure shattered like flowing sand and disappeared into the void in the blink of an eye.
Faustus and Camille exchanged a glance and remained silent for a long time.
That uninvited T6 Oracle-grade expert of the Chaos Humans had arrived without warning and left without the slightest reluctance.
But the things he had left behind had pushed both of their destinies forward by a tremendous margin!
Especially Camille.
From now on, he would no longer have to cross the river alone by feeling for stones.
As for the benefits Faustus had received, they were even more astonishing.
With the Chaos Black Soil in his hand, the final shortcoming of his Divine Domain could finally be filled.

The soul essence of the sage Angel King would serve as the core of Divinity. The World Origin Essence would nurture the spirit of the Divine Domain. Then, with the Chaos Black Soil as the foundation, he would solidify the roots of the Divine Domain.
Combined with that supreme Divine Domain, the Chaos Samsara Rank...
"I’ll absorb the Chaos Black Soil now."
Faustus unfolded his Divine Domain and tossed the unremarkable clump of soil into it.
The Chaos Black Soil was like melting amber, seeping bit by bit into the pair of distinct black-and-white eyes in the void.
The left eye represented life.
The right eye represented death.
Within the Divine Domain, the aura of chaos rose layer by layer, causing the surrounding space to tremble violently, like a sky that might collapse at any moment.
"My Divine Domain... is finally complete."
Faustus withdrew his Divine Domain, and a faint smile appeared on his face.
He had already pushed Holy Condensation to its limit long ago.
Now that his Divine Domain had reached grand perfection, it already possessed terrifying might no weaker than that of sage rank!
Together with his Endless Divine Power...
Even divine-grade experts could be fought.
Perhaps even... slain!
"Congratulations, Master, for finally refining your Divine Domain to perfection."
Camille sensed that aura, one that made him shudder from the depths of his bones, and he was deeply shaken.
Master had only stepped into supreme-grade a few days ago, yet he had already tempered his Divine Domain to such a level...
Master truly possessed peerless talent!
"Camille, you aren’t bad either."

Faustus smiled. "Now that you have that path of sword Dao advancement, with your foundation, breaking through to sage rank won’t be difficult. Once you cross that threshold, you will immediately reach the peak of divine-grade."
"I simply chose the right path!"
Camille smiled faintly. "I’ve realized that this sword Dao fits my own path as if they were cast from the same mold. Finally... I no longer need to worry about how to advance to sage."
Aetheria.
Faustus’s puppet avatar suddenly opened its eyes.
A streak of flowing light pierced through the air and arrived.
He reached out and seized that ray of light in his palm.
Faustus’s main body was stationed on Earth, while this puppet had been left here specifically to guard against the God Realm causing trouble.
He opened his hand. In his palm was a slip of paper.
"The Godkin intend to destroy Aetheria. Also, Kelly remains deep within the Bloodtide Sea of the God Realm."
Boom—!
A suffocating aura erupted from the puppet’s body.
"The Godkin... actually intend to destroy Aetheria!"
Killing intent surged in Faustus’s eyes.
Aetheria, like Earth, possessed a World Origin.
That was the most fragile and most vital thing in the entire world.
Once the Origin was destroyed, Aetheria would be completely finished.
That place held the greatest number of players, and the resurrection system would cease to exist as well.
Tens of billions of lives would die, and death would be final.
"They must be stopped."
At the same time, his gaze locked firmly onto the second half of the note.
Kelly...
She might still be alive!
And she was deep within the Bloodtide Sea of the God Realm.
Faustus clenched the slip of paper tightly, his knuckles tightening.
In the void.
A spatial passage suddenly opened wide.
Five Godkin experts walked out from within and stepped onto the land of Aetheria.
Their mission had only one objective: destroy Aetheria’s World Origin.
"Simon, where is the Origin Essence hidden?"
The leading expert turned his head, his tone filled with unquestionable urgency.

"The higher-ups said that Aetheria’s Origin is hidden extremely deeply. If we search for it bit by bit, who knows how long it’ll take? You have the treasure that can draw out the Origin Essence. Use it now."
Aetheria had existed for countless tens of thousands of years. Its Origin Essence had long since developed a will of its own and would never obediently wait to be captured.
As the race with the highest level of authority over this land, the Godkin naturally had a way to lure it out.
And that item was in Simon’s hands.
"Use it now?"
The corners of Simon’s lips rose slightly. Hidden within that smile was a meaning no one could see through.
"Nonsense. Are we supposed to turn this whole place upside down ourselves?"

"Don’t forget, we only have thirty minutes. After thirty minutes, the spatial passage will open one final time. If the mission isn’t complete by then, you can figure out how to get back to the God Realm on your own."
"Stop wasting time. Hurry up and draw out the Origin Essence."
"Exactly. Let’s finish the job quickly and leave."
The experts urged him one after another.
Simon sighed.
"Fine."
Before his words had even fully faded, his figure suddenly blurred, then solidified again.
In the blink of an eye, he had returned to his original position.
And the four Godkin experts collapsed to the ground one after another, as if the bones had been pulled out of their bodies. Their eyelids grew heavy, as though filled with lead.
Simon looked at them calmly and shook his head.
"This place is no longer safe."
He took out a treasure and activated it instantly.
Whoosh—!
The next moment, he disappeared without a trace, taking the four unconscious companions with him.
Faustus’s mind power spread outward like a tide, covering the entire land of Aetheria completely.
He did not know who had sent the note, and the note had not explained the whole story clearly either. He could only rely on himself to watch over everything.
As long as anything went wrong, he would discover it immediately.
"A spatial passage?"
As his mind power swept over a certain corner, that twisted spatial fissure immediately appeared in Faustus’s mind.
He took a deep breath.
In the next instant, he was already standing at the entrance of the passage.
He remembered the last time he had gone to the God Realm.
Back then, he had only been legendary-grade. He had not even possessed a Divine Domain.
Inside the sage rank of a divine-grade expert, he could only rely on self-destruction again and again to escape, forcing himself to trade the lives of the Godkin in the God Realm for his survival.
But now, things were different.
His main body was already a quasi-sage. He had condensed a supreme Divine Domain and possessed two secret arts specifically designed to counter sage rank.
This time, if he went to the God Realm again...
The ending would not be the same as last time.
"It would be impolite not to return the favor."
Faustus barely hesitated.
This time, he had to hurt the God Realm.
He had to hurt them so badly that they would never again dare to harbor crooked thoughts.
And there was also Kelly!
She might be in the Bloodtide Sea of the God Realm.
Although he did not know where the Bloodtide Sea was, once he arrived in the God Realm, he would find it eventually.
He leaped into the spatial passage.
"God Realm, I’m coming."
