chapters.title: Chapter 266 -266-The Top Three Seats Gather, Puppet Master
paragraphs: Just then—
Whoosh—!
Daniel’s figure appeared out of thin air.
Everyone had heard the name Faustus, but no one had ever seen what he looked like.
He glanced at the words "Westmoor Manor" on the gate, then walked straight inside.
"Friend, don’t go in yet! You’ll be blasted back out!"
A powerhouse kindly warned him.
"That’s right. The two inside are the ruthless ones ranked first and second."
"I think you’d better not go looking for trouble."
Daniel turned his head slightly and swept a calm glance over them. The corner of his mouth twitched faintly before he continued forward without looking back.
That arrogant demeanor immediately made the surrounding powerhouses burn with anger.
"What is he acting for? Does he think he’s Faustus or something? He’ll be crying soon enough!"
"This friend truly doesn’t know how to read the situation!"
"Hmph. Some people are just looking to die!"
A few powerhouses folded their arms across their chests, waiting to enjoy the show of Daniel being thrown out.
There were quite a few who shared that thought.
Raylor returned from the distance with a dark expression. He happened to see Daniel’s back as he stepped into Westmoor Manor.
"Where did this idiot come from? Is he tired of living?"
He spat coldly.
One minute passed...
There was no movement from inside.
Ten minutes passed...
Daniel’s figure still did not appear.
Twenty minutes passed...
The powerhouses waiting to watch the show completely exploded.
"I... Holy shit! That idiot from earlier actually didn’t get kicked out!?"
"No, wait. Who is that guy? Could he be an old acquaintance of those two inside?"
"Do you think there’s a possibility that the one just now was the Third Seat?"
"The Third Seat... is Faustus!"
The crowd of powerhouses exchanged glances.
Faustus had appeared!
He had entered Westmoor Manor.
At this moment, within Westmoor Manor, the top three powerhouses of the Starlight Rankings had gathered together for the first time.
The news spread like it had grown wings, sweeping wildly among the other twenty-seven participants.
"We misjudged him. That person was actually Faustus."
The powerhouses who had been waiting to see him embarrass himself felt as though they had been slapped in public.
"This Third Seat Faustus truly carries some weight."
Some powerhouses could not help comparing him to Raylor.
One had been blasted straight out, looking as miserable as a stray dog.
The other had swaggered inside and never come back out.
Who stood higher and who stood lower—did that even need to be said?
"Looks like that place inside has nothing to do with us."
Greatflow World was so barren that it made one feel suffocated. Only this manor was filled with MP so dense that it was practically a treasure land.
"The world of super prodigies really has no room for people like us."
Inside Westmoor Manor.
The moment Daniel stepped over the threshold, a violent aura rushed straight toward him.
A majestic wave of energy carrying killing intent came crashing at him.
Daniel raised an eyebrow. Elemental power surged in his palm and condensed into a fist, colliding fiercely with that figure.
Boom—!
That figure was smashed to pieces.
A palm-sized humanoid puppet floated down from midair. Its light was dim, and its body was covered in cracks.
The figure just now had actually been transformed from a puppet.
"Puppet Master?"
A trace of surprise flashed through Daniel’s eyes.
This secret art was rather interesting!
Whoosh—!
Something was tossed over from afar.
Daniel reached out and caught it steadily. The tip of his nose immediately picked up an extremely special fragrance.
It was rich and pure, yet not overpowering. Just smelling it gave him a sensation as though he were floating toward immortality.
[Ding! You have obtained Origin Essence +1,000 points!]
[Ding! You have obtained attribute points +1,000 points!]
Daniel had not even drunk it yet. Merely smelling the fragrance had already granted him such benefits.
If he drank it...
He lowered his head and looked at the small bottle in his hand. It was only as long as a middle finger.
Then he raised his head and drained it in one gulp.
The bottle looked small, but drinking from it felt as though he had swallowed a thousand liters of water.
The system notifications arrived as expected.
[Ding! You have obtained Origin Essence +10,000 points!]
[Ding! You have obtained attribute points +10,000 points!]
Daniel looked ahead, still wanting more.
"Hahaha—!"
Suddenly, laughter rang out inside the hall.
Daniel raised his eyes and saw two unfamiliar powerhouses come into view.
One black, one white.
The powerhouse in black robes was cold and stern, like an iceberg that had remained unmelted for ten thousand years.
The powerhouse in white was gentle and amiable, making others feel as though they were basking in a spring breeze.
The two sat facing one another, with a large pot suspended between them.
A blazing fire on the ground had burned the bottom of the pot red.
"Apologies, apologies."
The white-clothed powerhouse wore a sincere smile, his voice clear and refreshing.
"I am James. I enjoy peace and quiet, so I set up a little toy to keep idle people away. If I offended Your Excellency, please forgive me."
"No big deal."
Daniel did not care.
"That thing just now was pretty good. I am Faustus of the human race."
That strange liquid was far more than pretty good. It was simply top-grade!
When James heard the name Faustus, he showed no particular reaction. But when he heard Daniel praise that strange liquid, his eyes immediately lit up.
"As expected, Your Excellency Faustus has taste, unlike this idiot."
He shot a dissatisfied glance at Mosi sitting across from him.
"This fellow drank my wine and even complained that it tasted bad..."
After a brief pause, James invited him warmly.
"Your Excellency Faustus came at just the right time. This pot of thick soup is almost ready. Care to have a taste together?"
Faustus understood.
James, the First Seat. Mosi, the Second Seat. And himself, the Third Seat.
The three strongest beings on the Starlight Rankings had actually gathered together.
He could tell that James was sincere, so he did not put on airs. He walked over and sat down cross-legged.
The three of them formed a triangle around the bubbling pot in the middle.
Faustus glanced at Mosi and felt that the robe on him looked somewhat familiar.
Then he suddenly remembered the Luna_Fox assassin who had tried to assassinate him, only to be killed instead!
From that powerful assassin, he had obtained two extremely important secret arts.
"Do you recognize this?"
Faustus suddenly flipped his hand and took out a dagger. Its blade reflected a cold gleam under the firelight.
He looked at Mosi.
"Your attire looks very similar to the owner of this dagger."
James’ eyes lit up. He lifted his wine cup toward his mouth, but his ears immediately pricked up high.
"Of course."
Mosi’s voice was icy cold.
"I killed him."
Daniel’s tone was indifferent.
"Mm."
Mosi’s expression did not change. He did not even lift his eyelids.
"Do you want to avenge him?"
The corner of Daniel’s mouth rose slightly.
"No time."
Mosi answered very simply.
"Fine."
Daniel put the dagger away again.
The air suddenly fell silent, and the atmosphere became a little awkward.
"Haha... Since there’s no problem!"
James laughed and broke the stalemate.
"Then drink. Drink!"
He raised his wine cup and poured it toward his mouth.
But the wine never entered his throat at all. It all flowed down from the corners of his mouth, soaking the lower half of his face.
Strangely enough, two patches of red still appeared on his cheeks.
"I’ve been exposed."
James wiped his face and gave an embarrassed smile.
"This puppet secret art still hasn’t been cultivated properly."
So it turned out that the First Seat sitting before them was also nothing more than an incarnation.
His true body was hidden in some unknown corner.
Ignoring the thoughts of the other two, James pointed at the large pot.
"The soup is ready."
The instant the lid was lifted, a five-colored radiance shot into the sky, so dazzling that it made it impossible to open one’s eyes.
"Hm?"
Daniel’s gaze sharpened.
There was actually an aura within this light that felt familiar to him!

The instant the lid was lifted, a five-colored radiance shot into the sky, so dazzling that it made it impossible to open one’s eyes.
"Hm?"
Daniel’s gaze sharpened.
There was actually an aura within this light that felt familiar to him!

chapters.title: Chapter 267 -267-If You’re Unhappy, Let’s Fight
paragraphs: "This pot of soup is a super invincible limited edition!"
"To put it exaggeratedly, aside from me, there’s probably no one else who could make it."
James tilted his head back slightly, closed his eyes, and carefully inhaled the rising steam from the soup through his nose before speaking unhurriedly.
"There are two main special ingredients in this pot of soup. First is World Origin Essence, which I spent quite a bit of effort secretly intercepting from the Origin of Greatflow World!"
"Second is spirit vein essence. It’s right beneath the ground here, and even I only dared to draw out the tiniest strand."
Daniel listened very seriously.
He tried sending some of the soup into his mouth.
"This soup tastes really good. Delicious."
[Ding! attribute points +2,000!]
[Ding! attribute points +2,000!]
System notifications kept ringing beside Daniel’s ear, and he drank with even more enthusiasm.
Besides, the soup really was extremely delicious!
Mosi also took a stream of soup and drank it down.
"Not bad!"
Mosi coldly spat out two words.
James kept his eyes closed, a satisfied smile hanging on his face as he continued.

"I also added eight other rare treasure ingredients. This is the miraculous medicinal soup I personally concocted. With just one sip, you will understand what the most delicious food in the world truly is!"
He opened his eyes and smiled as he looked toward the soup pot.
However...
The pot was already empty!
Uh...
James’ smile froze on his face.
His eyes widened, and the corners of his eyes and mouth twitched violently.
A heaven-shaking aura suddenly erupted from his body!
No—!
Wails of agony rang out from Westmoor Manor.
The nearby powerhouses all turned their heads, completely confused.
There were only the top three seats inside Westmoor Manor. Judging from that sound, could it be...
"Did they start fighting?"
[Ding! You have obtained Origin Essence +100 points!]
[Ding! You have obtained Mental State +100 points!]
Hearing the sound beside his ear, Daniel directly sold them off.
[Ding! You have sold Origin Essence ×100 points to Doom Guild for 1 copper coin, triggering Millionfold Boost!]
[The item sold is a special energy-type item. Please choose quality boost / quantity boost!]
"Quantity boost!"
[Congratulations! You have obtained 1 gold coin! You have obtained [Origin Essence] ×10,000,000 points!]
[Ding! You have sold Mental State ×100 points to Doom Guild for 1 copper coin, triggering Millionfold Boost!]
[Congratulations! You have obtained Mental State +10,000,000 points!]
After drinking the soup and passing it through Millionfold Boost, Daniel’s gains had reached an astonishing level.
"This soup is incredible! If I could drink it every day..."
Daniel glanced at Mosi again.
That fellow looked cold and aloof, but in reality, he was not honest either. When they had been drinking the soup just now, he had not drunk any less.
At this moment, James felt uncomfortable all over.
He had painstakingly gathered the ingredients and spent a tremendous amount of effort simmering a pot of soup, yet he had not gotten a single sip himself.
He looked as though he had been struck by both a critical hit and a weakness curse at the same time. Listless and dispirited, he stared at Daniel and Mosi with resentful eyes.
"You two idiots... I regret this."
He gnashed his teeth.
Just then, Mosi looked at James and said coldly, "Then let’s fight."
"Aren’t you being far too shameless?"
James immediately shouted.
"You drank the soup I made, and now you want to use me as your sparring partner?"
"No matter how shameless someone is, they can’t order people around like you do!"
Daniel smiled as he watched the two of them bicker.
James and Mosi were clearly old acquaintances.
One was cold as ice, while the other looked gentle on the surface but was full of theatrics inside.
"Then shut up."
Mosi’s words were perfectly justified, concise, and direct.
"Come on, come on! Today, I’m going to beat every drop of soup you drank back out of you, then make you drink it again yourself!"
This time, James was truly heartbroken.
With a wave of his hand, another puppet flew out and transformed into his appearance!
"This guy’s puppets really are interesting!"
Daniel’s eyes lit up.
"Where exactly is his real body hidden? I actually can’t find it at all."
James was far too cautious.
No, rather, he was far too steady.
He was clearly absurdly powerful, yet he acted as cowardly as a rookie who had just walked out of Starter Village.
At some point, a blade had appeared in Mosi’s hand.
The blade was long and slender, and its scabbard was pitch-black.
A dark hand rested on the dark hilt.
He held the blade, but did not draw it.
He was gathering momentum!
The longer time passed, the heavier the dangerous aura on the blade became. The blade itself let out a low buzzing sound.
"A charged attack?"
Daniel remembered that there was such a school of thought on Earth, one that emphasized settling victory and defeat with a single slash.
Mosi’s version was a little different. He charged up first, and the longer he charged, the more terrifying the slash would be once unleashed.
Looking back at James, his second puppet lazily waved its hand, and a massive number of light shields instantly appeared around him.
Layer upon layer, densely packed together.
There had to be... several million layers!
"That many... shields?"
The corner of Daniel’s mouth twitched.
Several million layers of shields. Just how afraid of death was this man?
James sensed his gaze and explained in all seriousness.
"This world is too dangerous. One must be careful in all things..."
"Don’t be fooled by the fact that this secret art only has a few million shields on the surface."
James grew smug, as if he were showing off.
"In truth, I still have tens of millions hidden away."
"But whether or not they can block Mosi is still hard to say."
Then he frowned again and pretended to ponder.
"Looks like I need to modify it further and increase the external protective shields to over ten million. Only then will I have a little sense of security."
Daniel suddenly did not feel like speaking anymore.
"Did you develop this secret art yourself?"
he asked.
"Develop it myself? Are you joking?"
"I only improve things. I never create from scratch. Creating things myself is far too tiring."
James snorted and looked at Mosi.

"Only this idiot would tinker around with secret arts on his own. That charged slash of his is something he blindly messed around and created himself. It’s only a supreme-grade secret art. His aptitude is truly ordinary!"
Daniel fell silent.
Holy Condensation, Endless Divine Power, Immortal Icon, Void Annihilation...
Without the ten-thousandfold amplification system, all of those secret arts would only be supreme-grade.
And they had all been created by mighty beings at the Oracle-grade level.
To call a fellow who could create a supreme-grade secret art on his own and was clearly about to become a sage "ordinary in aptitude"?
"James."
Daniel sighed.
"I think I roughly understand why you’re so afraid of death."
"Hm?"
James looked utterly confused.
"With how much you show off, you must get struck by lightning pretty often, right?"
"It truly hasn’t been easy for you to survive until now."
James: "..."
"Are you even being polite?"
"But I do have one question... Why is it that supreme-grade secret arts are spread everywhere, but Divine-grade secret arts are rarely seen?"
Daniel asked.
James smiled and said, "Divine-grade secret arts contain traces of law power. They can only be comprehended by oneself and cannot be directly taught."

"Supreme-grade secret arts don’t have that restriction, so Divine-grade secret arts are especially rare. For quasi-sages like us, if we can master a Divine-grade secret art on our own before breaking through to sage, then once we advance to sage, we can directly rush to the peak of Divine-grade."
He glanced at Mosi.
"Mosi wants to walk that path."
"I’m different. I prefer stepping on the shoulders of those who came before me and climbing upward. Haha."
"So that’s how it is."
Daniel suddenly understood.
No wonder most of the secret arts he had obtained were supreme-grade, and only barely reached Divine-grade after Millionfold Boost.
So Divine-grade secret arts were actually that precious.
Moreover, as long as one studied and mastered a Divine-grade secret art by oneself, after breaking through, one could immediately stand at the highest point of Divine-grade.
No wonder even the sages of the God Realm used only supreme-grade secret arts rather than Divine-grade divine arts.
After all, the rules of the laws were there!
Right now, in the entirety of Aetheria, he was the only one standing on the stage of this starry sky.
As for the basic knowledge of the Endless Starsea, he barely understood anything at all.
In his previous lives, he had only been a small legendary-grade nobody. How could he have had the chance to come into contact with such things?
Only after hearing James explain it did he finally understand.
"He’s about ready."
James suddenly said.
"The terrifying thing about Mosi’s move isn’t just the blade. It’s Mosi himself."
Daniel looked toward Mosi.
He saw Mosi’s body wildly absorbing the energy accumulated within the scabbard. His entire body suddenly swelled to more than twice its original size!

chapters.title: Chapter 268 -268-Generous Friends, Sneaking Out
paragraphs: Shing—!
The saber left its sheath.
A flash of white light swept past, and nearly half of the millions of shield layers surrounding James vanished in the blink of an eye.
Boom!
Boom! Boom!
Mosi swung his saber and hacked wildly at James, every strike so violent that it bordered on madness.
James’s Puppet No. 2 could not even be bothered to move. It simply continued producing new shields, filling in the gaps as quickly as Mosi carved them open.
Daniel stared, dumbfounded.
"Mosi... is an assassin?"
Every time Mosi brought his saber down, cracks ripped through space itself.
This was clearly an insanely powerful, close-combat burst-type warrior. And they were telling him this man was an assassin?
"Of course. A top-class assassin, at that," James replied with a nod.
"The kind of assassin who kills his target in full view of everyone and considers the mission complete?"
Daniel felt as though he was beginning to understand.
"What is wrong with that?" James rubbed his nose. "If an assassin is going to kill someone, is it not better to do it as directly as possible?"
Daniel nodded thoughtfully.
"True enough... Seeing the target and killing them on the spot is certainly simpler than slowly searching for an opportunity."
The corners of his mouth twitched.
Just what kind of absurd paths had these two taken?
The assassins Daniel had imagined were supposed to slip unnoticed to their target’s side, kill them with a single strike, then disappear into the night without ever looking back.
They lurked in the shadows, came and went without a sound, and kept themselves so low-key that they practically became one with the dirt.
Yet now—
Daniel looked at the top-class assassin standing before him, Mosi, the second-ranked expert on the Starlight Rankings.
At this very moment, the man looked exactly like a berserk warrior.
Daniel shook his head.
Just then, Mosi suddenly sheathed his saber and stood there without the slightest expression on his face.
"Done already?"
James’s eyes lit up. He rubbed two fingers together, grinning like a fox that had just successfully stolen a chicken.
"Put it on my tab," Mosi said, spitting out only two words.
The smile on James’s face immediately froze.
"If you dare refuse to pay me back, I swear I will charge straight into Luna_Fox and beat you to death."
Mosi acted as though he had not heard him.
Whoosh—!
Puppet No. 2 turned into a streak of light and flew back into James’s body.
Daniel finally understood.
James was basically a nesting doll.
There was a clone inside a clone, and then another clone inside that clone.
More importantly, any random clone this fellow pulled out could probably pin an ordinary top expert to the ground and grind them into the dirt.
Greatflow World.
A group of experts from the Starlight Rankings had gathered together in secret, looking suspiciously furtive.

Hosek glanced around and found that everyone present was a familiar face. Lowering his voice, he said, "I just received news. They are currently arranging the list of participants for the Starlight Tournament!"
"The list of participants? Is there something special about it?"
Several experts looked confused.
"Hahaha..."
Hosek laughed slyly. "The waters involved here are very deep."
"You little bastard, stop keeping us in suspense and spit it out already."
"Exactly. You cannot just bait us like this."
Hosek pressed both hands downward, signaling everyone to calm down, then lowered his voice even further.

"The Starlight Rankings are only something we arranged among ourselves. The official participant list, however, has to be submitted to the organizers. The higher your name appears on that list, the more benefits you will receive."
"Should the strongest not simply be placed first?"
"Right. Can the order actually be changed?"
"Heh, it really can."
Hosek’s eyes lit up as he smiled. "As long as you are willing to pay a certain price, that list can be adjusted. As it happens, the faction behind me has precisely that sort of connection."
"Hiss—I remember now!"
"One of the major families of Gold-Grade Mountain stands behind you! No wonder!"
"But what benefit is there in changing our rankings?"
"Of course there are benefits."
A sharp glint flashed through Hosek’s eyes. "The higher your ranking is, the earlier you get to choose your opponent."
"Think about it. What kind of people are we about to fight?"

"The most terrifying top experts from every major starfield. If your ranking is too low and one of the top-ranked monsters from another starfield sets their eyes on you, then when the time comes, you will not even know where to go to cry."
Everyone nodded, finding his words rather reasonable.
"That is true. If we hold the initiative, we can simply choose the weakest among them. Would that not make our matches much safer?"
"Exactly. Looks like this list really is far more complicated than it appears."
Seeing that they were beginning to believe him, Hosek pressed on while the iron was hot.

"And that is not all. Think about it. If all of us squeeze into the front of the list, would that not serve as a smokescreen? The other starfields would not be able to determine which of us are truly strong and which are not. Would that not increase our chances of victory?"
"If we win, we live. If we lose, we die, my friends!"
Hosek urged them on. "What are you still waiting for? The list is about to be finalized. Once that happens, it will be too late even if you want to change it!"
His explanation made sense, and he also had the backing of his family. The eight or nine experts present were immediately tempted.
Everyone understood very clearly just how dangerous this tournament would be.
Being able to return alive would already count as a blessing.
If paying a small price to raise their positions on the list could improve their odds of survival, then no matter how they calculated it, it would be a worthwhile exchange.
"All right. I would like to give it a try."
"I am also willing to pay the price. So, what do you want?"
"Let me make this clear first. You can change your rankings if you want, but do not compete with me. I want first place!"
Several minutes later, Hosek watched the experts depart with a thoroughly satisfied smile.
"What a group of generous friends!"
He immediately contacted his family and began altering the order of participants.
Originally, the list had simply been arranged according to the Starlight Rankings. Gold-Grade Mountain did not care about this matter in the slightest.
As far as they were concerned, as long as everyone showed up, that was enough.
And Hosek had found the perfect loophole in that indifference.
"My dear friends, I never lied to any of you."
Hosek chuckled to himself.
The information he had gathered was true: those whose names ranked higher really did gain priority when choosing their opponents!
But if people from Greatflow World could change their rankings, could the other starfields not do the same?
Several days later.
Westmoor Manor.
By now, Daniel had become quite familiar with the other two.
At this moment, the three of them were gathered together.
"Lord Faustus, Brother Mosi..."
James looked at the two puppets in his hands and smiled.
"Would sneaking out really be that difficult? Our true bodies may be unable to move, but my puppetry can carry the mind power of both of you outside."
Daniel raised an eyebrow and said indifferently, "Enough nonsense. Get straight to the point and tell us how to do it."
After spending the past few days together, Daniel had more or less figured out James’s personality.
This fellow was quite interesting, but he simply could not control his mouth.
He had no shortage of bizarre and brilliant ideas, but one must never give him the chance to get carried away. The moment he started floating, he would never come back down.
As for Mosi...
He was genuinely a man who treasured words as though they were gold. If he could express himself with one word, he would never waste a second. On top of that, he was born with a face as cold as ice.
"Speak," Mosi said coldly, squeezing out a single word.

James did not mind in the slightest. Smiling cheerfully, he continued, "You two only need to condense a portion of your mind power and attach it to my puppets. After that, Mosi can use his mastery of the Law of Space to take us through the world barrier. Would that not allow us to get out?"
Swish! Swish—!
Daniel and Mosi snatched the two puppets out of James’s hands with astonishing speed.
James could not help muttering inwardly.
Did the two of you really have to be this impatient?
In the blink of an eye, three fresh new substitutes were born: Faustus No. 2, Mosi No. 2, and James No. 2.

"I have a suggestion," James said. "Once we get outside, we split up and search for those Astral Corsairs separately. Whoever subdues the most sages becomes the big brother. Whoever subdues the fewest becomes the little brother."
"No problem," Daniel agreed immediately.
"Fine."
Mosi, surprisingly, even nodded.
"It is up to you, then."
James lifted his chin toward Mosi.
Swish—!
Mosi’s attainments in the Law of Space were extremely profound. Passing through the world barrier was as effortless for him as strolling through an empty courtyard.
Carrying the two puppets with him, he slipped into the void and silently flew out of Greatflow World.
Meanwhile, the true bodies of the three experts remained inside Westmoor Manor.
Their true bodies had never taken so much as half a step outside Greatflow World.
Surely that did not count as breaking the rules, right?
There was absolutely nothing wrong with that.
And taking ten thousand steps back, even if they were discovered, so what?
These three occupied the top three seats on the Starlight Rankings.
At a critical moment like this, if Gold-Grade Mountain truly provoked them into anger, it would never be able to bear the consequences!

Hosek glanced around and found that everyone present was a familiar face.
Lowering his voice, he said, "I just received news.
They are currently arranging the list of participants for the Starlight Tournament!"
"The list of participants?
Is there something special about it?"
Several experts looked confused.
"Hahaha..."
Hosek laughed slyly.
"The waters involved here are very deep."
"You little bastard, stop keeping us in suspense and spit it out already."
"Exactly.
You cannot just bait us like this."
Hosek pressed both hands downward, signaling everyone to calm down, then lowered his voice even further.
"The Starlight Rankings are only something we arranged among ourselves.
The official participant list, however, has to be submitted to the organizers.
The higher your name appears on that list, the more benefits you will receive."
"Should the strongest not simply be placed first?"
"Right.
Can the order actually be changed?"
"Heh, it really can."
Hosek’s eyes lit up as he smiled.
"As long as you are willing to pay a certain price, that list can be adjusted.
As it happens, the faction behind me has precisely that sort of connection."
"Hiss—I remember now!"
"One of the major families of Gold-Grade Mountain stands behind you!
No wonder!"
"But what benefit is there in changing our rankings?"
"Of course there are benefits."
A sharp glint flashed through Hosek’s eyes.
"The higher your ranking is, the earlier you get to choose your opponent."
"Think about it.
What kind of people are we about to fight?"
"The most terrifying top experts from every major starfield.
If your ranking is too low and one of the top-ranked monsters from another starfield sets their eyes on you, then when the time comes, you will not even know where to go to cry."
Everyone nodded, finding his words rather reasonable.
"That is true.
If we hold the initiative, we can simply choose the weakest among them.
Would that not make our matches much safer?"
"Exactly.
Looks like this list really is far more complicated than it appears."
Seeing that they were beginning to believe him, Hosek pressed on while the iron was hot.
"And that is not all.
Think about it.
If all of us squeeze into the front of the list, would that not serve as a smokescreen?
The other starfields would not be able to determine which of us are truly strong and which are not.
Would that not increase our chances of victory?"
"If we win, we live.
If we lose, we die, my friends!"
Hosek urged them on.
"What are you still waiting for?
The list is about to be finalized.
Once that happens, it will be too late even if you want to change it!"
His explanation made sense, and he also had the backing of his family.
The eight or nine experts present were immediately tempted.
Everyone understood very clearly just how dangerous this tournament would be.
Being able to return alive would already count as a blessing.
If paying a small price to raise their positions on the list could improve their odds of survival, then no matter how they calculated it, it would be a worthwhile exchange.
"All right.
I would like to give it a try."
"I am also willing to pay the price.
So, what do you want?"
"Let me make this clear first.
You can change your rankings if you want, but do not compete with me.
I want first place!"
Several minutes later, Hosek watched the experts depart with a thoroughly satisfied smile.
"What a group of generous friends!"
He immediately contacted his family and began altering the order of participants.
Originally, the list had simply been arranged according to the Starlight Rankings.
Gold-Grade Mountain did not care about this matter in the slightest.
As far as they were concerned, as long as everyone showed up, that was enough.
And Hosek had found the perfect loophole in that indifference.
"My dear friends, I never lied to any of you."
Hosek chuckled to himself.
The information he had gathered was true: those whose names ranked higher really did gain priority when choosing their opponents!
But if people from Greatflow World could change their rankings, could the other starfields not do the same?
Several days later.
Westmoor Manor.
By now, Daniel had become quite familiar with the other two.
At this moment, the three of them were gathered together.
"Lord Faustus, Brother Mosi..."
James looked at the two puppets in his hands and smiled.
"Would sneaking out really be that difficult?
Our true bodies may be unable to move, but my puppetry can carry the mind power of both of you outside."
Daniel raised an eyebrow and said indifferently, "Enough nonsense.
Get straight to the point and tell us how to do it."
After spending the past few days together, Daniel had more or less figured out James’s personality.
This fellow was quite interesting, but he simply could not control his mouth.
He had no shortage of bizarre and brilliant ideas, but one must never give him the chance to get carried away.
The moment he started floating, he would never come back down.
As for Mosi...
He was genuinely a man who treasured words as though they were gold.
If he could express himself with one word, he would never waste a second.
On top of that, he was born with a face as cold as ice.
"Speak," Mosi said coldly, squeezing out a single word.
James did not mind in the slightest.
Smiling cheerfully, he continued, "You two only need to condense a portion of your mind power and attach it to my puppets.
After that, Mosi can use his mastery of the Law of Space to take us through the world barrier.
Would that not allow us to get out?"
Swish!
Swish—!
Daniel and Mosi snatched the two puppets out of James’s hands with astonishing speed.
James could not help muttering inwardly.
Did the two of you really have to be this impatient?
In the blink of an eye, three fresh new substitutes were born: Faustus No.
2, Mosi No.
2, and James No.
"I have a suggestion," James said.
"Once we get outside, we split up and search for those Astral Corsairs separately.
Whoever subdues the most sages becomes the big brother.
Whoever subdues the fewest becomes the little brother."
"No problem," Daniel agreed immediately.
"Fine."
Mosi, surprisingly, even nodded.
"It is up to you, then."
James lifted his chin toward Mosi.
Swish—!
Mosi’s attainments in the Law of Space were extremely profound.
Passing through the world barrier was as effortless for him as strolling through an empty courtyard.
Carrying the two puppets with him, he slipped into the void and silently flew out of Greatflow World.
Meanwhile, the true bodies of the three experts remained inside Westmoor Manor.
Their true bodies had never taken so much as half a step outside Greatflow World.
Surely that did not count as breaking the rules, right?
There was absolutely nothing wrong with that.
And taking ten thousand steps back, even if they were discovered, so what?
These three occupied the top three seats on the Starlight Rankings.
At a critical moment like this, if Gold-Grade Mountain truly provoked them into anger, it would never be able to bear the consequences!

chapters.title: Chapter 269 -269- The Ambusher Gets Ambushed
paragraphs: Mosi No. 2 led the two "stand-ins" out of Greatflow World.
The three of them had already agreed upon a time and place to meet again. Once they emerged, they immediately split up and went about their respective missions.
As Daniel flew toward the rendezvous point, he could barely suppress the smug laughter rising in his heart.
Those two idiots could run all over the starry skies subduing Astral Corsairs to their hearts’ content!
As for him, he would simply wait at the meeting point.
Once they had gone through all the trouble of dragging a whole crowd of new underlings back with them, he would swoop in and steal the fruits of their labor.
How convenient was that?
Simple. Crude. Direct.
That was the true path of kings!
Besides, this would be the perfect opportunity to weigh James and Mosi’s true abilities.
Just how strong had the two of them actually become?
And by comparison, exactly how far ahead of them was he?
After all, his own strength had risen at a somewhat ridiculous rate recently.
Even Daniel himself was beginning to find it a little absurd.
The appointed time passed in the blink of an eye.
In the distant void, a Star Island slowly drifted into view.
The people standing upon the Star Island were clearly divided into two groups.
On one side stood Mosi, his face as cold and expressionless as ever.
On the other side stood a thoroughly miserable-looking band of pirates.
Among them were several low-grade Sages, a number of Demi-Sages, and an enormous crowd of lesser minions. All together, there were several thousand of them.
At this moment, however, this fearsome pirate force was huddled together like frightened livestock, their bodies trembling uncontrollably.
Every now and then, they cast terrified glances at the icy figure standing ahead of them.
That monster was simply too powerful!
Even the Sages among them had been no different from helpless chicks in front of him. They had not possessed the slightest ability to fight back.
"Our Black Starsea Pirate Crew was actually... robbed?"
"What kind of sick joke is this?"
"This can’t be real. Tell me I’m still dreaming!"
"I feel like we’ve completely disgraced the name of the Astral Corsairs..."
The Star Island continued floating forward through the darkness.
What none of the pirates noticed was that, hidden in the shadows of the surrounding void, a pair of eyes had already fixed firmly upon them.
"They’re here?"
"It’s Mosi."
A playful smile appeared on James’s face.
As it turned out, he had never gone far in the first place. He had been lurking nearby the entire time, patiently waiting for an opportunity to snatch someone else’s harvest.
And now, after all that waiting, Mosi had finally arrived.
"Hmm... I can’t be too reckless. Better play it safe first."
James called his third puppet back to his side, then ordered it to transform into Daniel’s appearance.
In the blink of an eye, another "Daniel" stood before him.
"Brother Mosi, here I come!"
The fake Daniel flashed a broad grin. Then, with a flicker of movement, he vanished into the void.
On the Star Island, Mosi suddenly lifted his eyelids.
A sharp gleam flashed through his eyes.
"Hmph."
He gave a cold snort in response.
At that exact moment—
Boom!
The fake Daniel abruptly emerged from the void and blocked the Star Island’s path.
"Mosi!" he shouted arrogantly. "I’ve been sick of looking at that foul expression of yours every single day!"
"Today, I’m going to beat some manners into you!"
His voice boomed across the void, his manner so overbearing that he seemed completely convinced of his own invincibility.
Mosi did not say a word.
His figure merely blurred.
Then he disappeared from where he stood.
By the time he reappeared, he was already behind the fake Daniel.
Draw blade.
Slash!
That was Mosi’s answer.
A heaven-shaking blade light erupted from his weapon, its terrible radiance making it seem as though the very sky above them had collapsed.
Boom! Boom!
The two figures collided violently in midair.
The fake Daniel was sent flying by a single slash, yet even as he tumbled backward, he continued shouting at the top of his lungs.
"Is that all you’ve got?!"
"Come on! Keep going!"
The moment he finished yelling, he turned around and fled without the slightest hesitation.
Mosi’s eyelids drooped halfway, giving him the appearance of someone who had not fully awakened from sleep.
Then, without the slightest delay, he chased after him.
Meanwhile, no one noticed that another figure had appeared aboard the Star Island at some point.
It was none other than James.
The pirate crew immediately stirred.
A number of them exchanged glances, their eyes gradually revealing wolf-like ferocity.
That ice-cold demon had finally left.
And now, in his place, some ordinary-looking fellow had appeared.
Perhaps this was their chance!
Perhaps they could—
Boom!
Before they could act, James’s aura suddenly erupted in full force.
Terrifying pressure crashed down upon the entire Star Island like a descending mountain.
James stared coldly at the mass of pirates.
"Do as you’re told if you want to live."
The fierce flames that had only just begun to burn in the pirates’ hearts were instantly extinguished.
"Holy shit! Why is this guy just as terrifying?!"
"No, seriously, what is wrong with this part of the starry skies? Why are all these Demi-Sages so unbelievably monstrous?"
"Hiss... Just what kind of terrible luck are we having?"
"This is definitely because Old Matt stole a portion of the Origin from that life-bearing world a while back! We must have been cursed because of him!"
"Bullshit! With my strength, how could I possibly pull off something like that? I might as well say you got cursed because you pissed against the wind!"
"Damn you! What does that have to do with anything?!"
The pirates were on the verge of collapsing into despair.
They had originally believed themselves to be seasoned predators of the starry seas, feared wherever they went.
Yet today, they had somehow transformed into a pile of helpless goods being passed from one terrifying monster to another.
James ignored their muttering completely.
"Mosi, Mosi..." he thought with a quiet chuckle. "You’re still too young."
"These little brothers of yours are mine now."
"Just consider it repayment for what you owe me."
He waved his hand grandly.
"Pirate crew, set off!"
Under James’s control, the Star Island immediately accelerated, racing at full speed toward the appointed meeting point.
However, not long after the Star Island disappeared into the distance, the surrounding void suddenly rippled.
A spatial crack quietly opened.
From within it, Mosi’s figure slowly emerged.
There was a faint hint of mockery in his eyes.
"Idiot."
He coldly spat out those two words.
At the rendezvous point stood an abandoned planet.
Daniel’s mind power had long since spread out like an enormous net, completely covering the surrounding region.
Thus, the instant the Star Island approached, its movements were immediately caught within his perception.
At the same time, James also noticed that his trail had entered someone else’s mind power range.
His expression instantly changed.
"Something’s wrong!"
"That shameless bastard Faustus is cheating!"
"How can he be this despicable?!"
Boom!
Before James could complain any further, Daniel’s figure suddenly materialized directly in front of the speeding Star Island.
His battle intent surged into the heavens.
"James, come and fight me!"
"Who’s afraid of you?!"
James gritted his teeth fiercely and charged out from the Star Island.
At the same instant, the millions upon millions of protective shields covering his body all activated at once.
Layer after layer of radiant defenses bloomed around him, stacking so thickly that they appeared almost endless.
"Immortal Icon!"
Daniel roared.
His body instantly expanded, growing larger and larger until he had transformed into an enormous giant towering between heaven and earth.
Then his gigantic fist came crashing down like a falling meteor.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
Daniel’s monstrous fist tore through James’s wall of shields with an unstoppable momentum.
Those millions of protective barriers, which ought to have been enough to make any ordinary opponent despair, were pierced through as though they had been made of paper.
One layer after another burst apart.
In a matter of moments, the supposedly impenetrable defensive wall had been violently demolished.
"Destiny—Law of Causality!"
This punch was destined to strike its target!
James clenched his teeth.
He could clearly feel an invisible force locking firmly onto him. No matter how he moved or where he tried to flee, escaping this blow was impossible.
It was as though the result had already been written into fate itself.
James instantly understood.
This had to be the power of some immensely profound law.
"What the hell? This Faustus is way too strong!"
Since dodging was no longer an option, James simply stopped trying.
Several puppets flew out from his sleeves and instantly transformed into identical copies of himself.
James had begun stacking substitutes inside substitutes once more.
Boom!
Daniel’s enormous fist descended without the slightest suspense and pulverized James’s body on the spot.
Yet in the next instant, another James appeared in the surrounding void, grinning as though nothing had happened.
Daniel’s eyes curved faintly with amusement.
"You want to compete with me using clones?"
With a thought, ninety-nine identical figures appeared around him in an instant.
Each one possessed the exact same appearance and an equally terrifying aura.
"James, tremble before me!"
The ninety-nine clones attacked simultaneously, unleashing their strongest techniques from every direction.
"Void Annihilation!"
"Immortal Icon!"
"Chaos Samsara Rank—Activate!"
Violent energies exploded throughout the void.
Daniel’s clones and James’s clones crashed into each other, instantly plunging the entire region into a chaotic battlefield.
Every collision sent powerful shock waves rolling through the starry skies.
Fragments of shattered energy scattered outward like exploding stars.
Yet even under Daniel’s overwhelming assault, James continued smiling.
"The outcome hasn’t been decided yet."
Suddenly, every single one of James’s clones opened his Divine Domain at the same time.
James’s Divine Domain was extremely strange.
It was a hole.
A pitch-black, bottomless hole that seemed capable of swallowing all things.
No matter what techniques Daniel released, the moment they approached that black hole, they disappeared without leaving even the faintest trace behind.
They were not shattered.
They were not blocked.
They were simply erased, as though the attacks had never existed in the first place.
"The Law of Creation!"
Daniel possessed the Law of Causality.
Mosi possessed the Law of Space.
And James, naturally, possessed his own law as well.
This law was likewise one of the supreme laws that towered above countless ordinary laws.
The black hole formed within James’s Divine Domain was condensed from the Law of Creation itself.
By wielding the power of creation, he had actually managed to forcibly hold off Daniel’s Destiny Law of Causality.
Even Daniel could not help feeling slightly impressed.
James truly deserved his reputation.
However, admiration was one thing.
Showing mercy was another.
"Chaos Samsara—Activate!"
Daniel’s Divine Domain abruptly unfolded.
The entire void trembled violently.
Then, within the endless darkness, a pair of enormous eyes suddenly opened.
One was black.
The other was white.
The powers of black and white reincarnation intertwined and merged together, transforming into an enormous monochrome scroll.
The instant the scroll formed, it spread outward and enveloped James completely.
What shocked James even more was that the scroll pierced straight through his Divine Domain in an instant.
His black hole could not devour it.
His Law of Creation could not stop it.
His expression finally froze.
"A Reincarnation Divine Domain..."
James could feel his life force rapidly draining away.
His heart tightened in alarm.
"Are you kidding me?"
"A single Divine Domain actually contains the power of two separate laws?"
"How is anyone supposed to fight against something like this?!"
It happened almost instantly.
Every single one of James’s clones lost the ability to maintain its transformation and reverted back into puppets.
The false bodies collapsed one after another, scattering helplessly through the void.
"Stop! Stop!"
James’s voice drifted out from somewhere within empty space, filled with obvious frustration and defeat.
"I surrender."
A moment later, James emerged from the void with a thoroughly dejected expression.
He sighed heavily.
"Faustus, that Divine Domain of yours is simply too ridiculous. I concede defeat completely."
Daniel withdrew his Divine Domain.
The corners of his lips lifted slightly, carrying the faint smile of a victor who had fully expected this outcome from the beginning.
"You’re not bad either."
His voice was calm and composed.
"The top-ranked genius on the Starlight Rankings truly lives up to his reputation."
Hearing such exaggerated "praise," even someone as shameless as James could not help feeling a little embarrassed.
His face reddened slightly.
Still, Daniel quickly added in a far more sincere tone, "But speaking seriously, your Divine Domain really is extraordinary."
Then he paused.
"It is merely a tiny bit inferior to mine."
The moment James heard that, most of the gloom on his face instantly vanished.
A wide grin abruptly returned to his face.
"Then what about Mosi?"
Daniel’s lips curved upward.
He did not answer immediately.
Instead, he raised one hand.
Elemental power surged and gathered within his palm, rapidly condensing into the shape of a long spear.
The spear was woven from both ice and flame.

Dark blue radiance flowed along one side of its body, while blazing crimson light surged along the other. The opposing forces twisted together without conflict, releasing an aura of destruction so terrifying that it made one’s heart tremble.
Whoosh!
Daniel hurled the spear forward.
It shot through the void like a meteor piercing the sun, violently stabbing into an apparently empty region of space.
The astonishing force contained within it instantly tore apart the outermost layer of space.
The void split open like a curtain being ripped apart by an invisible hand, cracks spreading rapidly in every direction.
Boom!
A figure was forcibly blasted out from within the spatial rift.
It was none other than Mosi!

This law was likewise one of the supreme laws that towered above countless ordinary laws.
The black hole formed within James’s Divine Domain was condensed from the Law of Creation itself.
By wielding the power of creation, he had actually managed to forcibly hold off Daniel’s Destiny Law of Causality.
Even Daniel could not help feeling slightly impressed.
James truly deserved his reputation.
However, admiration was one thing.
Showing mercy was another.
"Chaos Samsara—Activate!"
Daniel’s Divine Domain abruptly unfolded.
The entire void trembled violently.
Then, within the endless darkness, a pair of enormous eyes suddenly opened.
One was black.
The other was white.
The powers of black and white reincarnation intertwined and merged together, transforming into an enormous monochrome scroll.
The instant the scroll formed, it spread outward and enveloped James completely.
What shocked James even more was that the scroll pierced straight through his Divine Domain in an instant.
His black hole could not devour it.
His Law of Creation could not stop it.
His expression finally froze.
"A Reincarnation Divine Domain..."
James could feel his life force rapidly draining away.
His heart tightened in alarm.
"Are you kidding me?"
"A single Divine Domain actually contains the power of two separate laws?"
"How is anyone supposed to fight against something like this?!"
It happened almost instantly.
Every single one of James’s clones lost the ability to maintain its transformation and reverted back into puppets.
The false bodies collapsed one after another, scattering helplessly through the void.
"Stop!
Stop!"
James’s voice drifted out from somewhere within empty space, filled with obvious frustration and defeat.
"I surrender."
A moment later, James emerged from the void with a thoroughly dejected expression.
He sighed heavily.
"Faustus, that Divine Domain of yours is simply too ridiculous.
I concede defeat completely."
Daniel withdrew his Divine Domain.
The corners of his lips lifted slightly, carrying the faint smile of a victor who had fully expected this outcome from the beginning.
"You’re not bad either."
His voice was calm and composed.
"The top-ranked genius on the Starlight Rankings truly lives up to his reputation."
Hearing such exaggerated "praise," even someone as shameless as James could not help feeling a little embarrassed.
His face reddened slightly.
Still, Daniel quickly added in a far more sincere tone, "But speaking seriously, your Divine Domain really is extraordinary."
Then he paused.
"It is merely a tiny bit inferior to mine."
The moment James heard that, most of the gloom on his face instantly vanished.
A wide grin abruptly returned to his face.
"Then what about Mosi?"
Daniel’s lips curved upward.
He did not answer immediately.
Instead, he raised one hand.
Elemental power surged and gathered within his palm, rapidly condensing into the shape of a long spear.
The spear was woven from both ice and flame.
Dark blue radiance flowed along one side of its body, while blazing crimson light surged along the other.
The opposing forces twisted together without conflict, releasing an aura of destruction so terrifying that it made one’s heart tremble.
Whoosh!
Daniel hurled the spear forward.
It shot through the void like a meteor piercing the sun, violently stabbing into an apparently empty region of space.
The astonishing force contained within it instantly tore apart the outermost layer of space.
The void split open like a curtain being ripped apart by an invisible hand, cracks spreading rapidly in every direction.
Boom!
A figure was forcibly blasted out from within the spatial rift.
It was none other than Mosi!

chapters.title: Chapter 270 -270-Starlit Gala, Dawn Pirates
paragraphs: Mosi had, in fact, been hiding in the shadows the entire time.
He had never truly been lured away by the fake Daniel. He had merely pretended to give chase, while in reality remaining concealed within this stretch of the void all along.
He knew that fellow James would not be smug for long.
Sure enough, Daniel and James had ended up fighting each other.
Meanwhile, Mosi had remained hidden, lying patiently in wait for the perfect opportunity to make his move.
Unfortunately, what irritated him greatly was that Daniel always seemed capable of sensing his presence through some mysterious instinct.
Those eyes of his were as though they could pierce through the void itself. No matter how deeply Mosi concealed himself, he could never truly hide from Daniel’s gaze.
Mosi’s hand had already settled upon the hilt of his blade.
"Oh?" Daniel asked softly. "You still wish to fight?"
Before his words had even faded, ninety-nine clones surged out like a tide, surrounding Mosi from every direction.
"Fight."
Mosi coldly spat out a single word.
One minute later...
Mosi stood there with a bruised and swollen face, his voice hoarse and strained.
"I surrender."
Even in such a miserable state, however, his face remained utterly devoid of expression.
Only then did Daniel withdraw his Divine Domain and dismiss his clones. Smiling, he asked, "Convinced now?"
The dispirited James and the battered Mosi looked at one another, both at a loss for words.
"I have always been a man who convinces others through reason. I never force people to do things against their will."
"What I love most in this world is having a calm and reasonable discussion."
Daniel spoke with a beaming smile.
"I’m convinced!"
The instant James noticed that Daniel seemed inclined to start another "discussion," he hurriedly lowered his head and admitted defeat.
"Convinced."
Mosi likewise helplessly squeezed out a single word.
The sky looked as though it had been ripped open by an invisible giant hand.
One figure after another streaked through the cloud layer, the trails of light behind them carving brief arcs across the darkened sky before vanishing in an instant.
On the ground below, the players craned their necks upward, watching those flying figures with envy and admiration in their eyes.
Those were the supreme experts they had long looked up to from afar.
"That person who just flew past... was Skylight!"
Someone suddenly cried out in shock.
"That’s right! He’s the super expert who has held second place on the rankings for years!"
"Sunborn is here too! He’s always ranked steadily in third place!"
"Why are so many peak-level experts all flying in the same direction? Could some terrifying ancient beast have appeared over there?"
The ordinary players were abuzz with speculation.
To them, any one of those figures soaring through the sky was an existence they could only dream of approaching.
Yet now, so many of the strongest players in the entire world had appeared at once.
Something extraordinary was clearly about to happen.
A massive starship hung steadily in the void.
Its cabin doors slid open without a sound.
Carodion stood expressionlessly at the entrance, carefully identifying every player who entered.
These were all individuals who normally commanded the winds and summoned the rain on the rankings, renowned powerhouses whose names were familiar to almost every player in the world.
Yet at this moment, each of them was suppressing the excitement in his or her chest as they filed obediently into the starship.
When the final player stepped through the cabin entrance, Carodion finally turned around and walked farther into the vessel, soon arriving before Camille.
"My lord, everyone has arrived."
"Depart."
Camille nodded slightly, his voice deep and solemn.
Rumble! Rumble!
The gigantic vessel’s energy systems activated in an instant.
Dark blue flames erupted from its engines.
The entire battleship trembled violently, like an ancient beast that had slumbered for countless ages finally breaking free of its chains.
In the next moment, it shot out of the plane at astonishing speed, charging toward the boundless starry skies beyond the world.
Not long ago, Daniel had issued an order.
The top fifty players on the world’s level rankings were to assemble and board a massive starship, traveling to a certain destination to participate in a grand gathering among the stars.
Every one of these players was around Level 300.
They belonged to the very small group of people standing at the absolute summit of this world.
When they had first received the news, they had been so stunned that they could not speak for a long while.
They were going to experience the Starlit Gala!
How unbelievable was that?
All this time, the Endless Starsea had existed only in their wildest fantasies.
It was a boundless place beyond their world, a mysterious expanse filled with unknown civilizations, foreign races, terrifying experts, and opportunities beyond imagination.
Now, they were finally about to enter it personally.
"Do you think every living creature we encounter from now on counts as an alien?"
"Tsk, tsk... Aliens! Mom, your son has finally made something of himself!"
"What level of power does Legendary-Grade count as in the Endless Starsea?"
"The Starlit Gala... Damn, I’m getting excited just thinking about it!"
"Who cares how strong we are out there? At least we’ll be among the first players ever to set foot in the stars!"
The players were unusually excited, their hearts surging like violent waves.
They crowded around the transparent portholes, staring outside with burning curiosity.
However, all that remained in their field of vision was endless darkness.
That was the color produced when space itself was folded and traversed at tremendous speed.
The starship was already carrying them toward a world far beyond anything they had ever known.
On the abandoned planet, Daniel had used his iron fists to make both James and Mosi acknowledge his position as their boss.
Relying on his absurdly thick skin, James successfully seized the second-highest position in their little organization.
Mosi, unable to do anything about it, could only resign himself to becoming the third brother.
With two brand-new rookies of the pirate world now following behind him, Daniel formally embarked on his journey.
In only a short period of time, the three powerful experts used their overwhelming strength to conquer pirate crew after pirate crew.
Anyone who dared resist was promptly beaten into submission.
Anyone with a little more sense immediately surrendered before the beating even began.
At present, Daniel’s forces already controlled five Star Islands.
Under his command were three Low-Grade Sages, five Demi-Sages, more than a thousand Supreme-Grade experts, and countless God-Grade subordinates!
After giving the matter some simple thought, Daniel casually settled upon a name for his newly established force.
The Dawn Pirates.
Before long, the name of the Dawn Pirates began spreading throughout this region of the starry river.
At first, the surrounding pirate crews had only heard scattered rumors.
A mysterious new pirate faction had appeared out of nowhere.
Its leader was terrifyingly powerful.
The two monsters following him were nearly as unreasonable.
Wherever the three of them went, established pirate crews were crushed one after another and forcibly absorbed into their ranks.
Soon, those rumors became impossible to ignore.
The Dawn Pirates were no longer merely an unknown group of newcomers.
They had become a rapidly rising force whose name was beginning to carry real weight throughout the surrounding starry skies.
Just then, a massive starship slowly descended upon one of the Star Islands.
The hatch opened.
Several dozen peak-level players filed out in succession.
The instant they saw the familiar figure waiting ahead of them, their faces lit up with excitement.
"It’s the Guildmaster!"
"Boss Guildmaster!"
"Guildmaster Boss, I finally get to see you again! You’re still as handsome as ever!"
"Guildmaster, you actually became a pirate before us? That’s way too unfair!"
Voices rang out one after another.
Daniel smiled and nodded in greeting.
They were all familiar faces. Everyone here had known one another for a long time already, so there was no need for unnecessary ceremony.
"Welcome to your first arrival in the Endless Starsea."
Daniel’s voice was not loud, but it clearly entered the ears of every player present.
"For the time being, you will remain here as trainee pirates. Once you have spent some time in this place, you will naturally understand what the starry skies are truly like."
The moment these words left his mouth, all the players froze.
"Pirates? Trainees?"
"The Guildmaster really knows how to have fun... Why do I suddenly feel like something isn’t quite right?"
"Hold on, do trainee pirates get experience points and wages?"
"More importantly, is there any danger allowance?"
"Can we rob other pirates? Or are we the ones getting robbed?"
"Judging from the Guildmaster’s expression, I have a feeling we’re about to be assigned a ridiculous amount of work..."
The players immediately began whispering among themselves.
A moment ago, they had still been fantasizing about exploring the glorious mysteries of the Endless Starsea.
Now, without warning, they had apparently become pirate interns.
Their grand interstellar adventure had taken an unexpectedly strange turn.
Daniel ignored their complaints after arranging everything.
His purpose in bringing these players here was to allow them to adapt to the Endless Starsea in advance.
Their identity as pirates was only temporary.
Once they had become sufficiently accustomed to the environment and dangers of the starry skies, he would gradually expand the scale of this operation and allow more players to take part.
With several Sages overseeing the situation, their safety could barely be considered acceptable.
Besides, even if the players died, they could still revive. The only inconvenience was that they would be sent back to their bound revival points.
At present, the players’ rate of growth was still far too slow.
Daniel hoped that by entering the Endless Starsea, they would be able to temper themselves more thoroughly and obtain more opportunities.
After all, opportunities within the stars were as countless as the stars themselves.
Danger existed everywhere.
But so did fortune.
An unknown amount of time later.
Greatflow World.
At a certain location in the void, space suddenly began to distort.
It looked as though an invisible giant hand had seized hold of the fabric of space and was slowly twisting it.
Gradually, a deep and mysterious vortex took shape.
It was a teleportation gate capable of crossing entire starfields.
Then, that vast and majestic voice rang out once more.
"The tournament is about to begin. All participants are to pass through the teleportation gate immediately and proceed to the Budelica Starfield!"
The venue of the Starlight Tournament was none other than the Budelica Starfield.
This was not some minor contest confined to a corner of the Canaan Starfield.
It was a magnificent event jointly organized by eight great starfields!
A supreme competition involving the finest young prodigies across the entire universe!
Daniel, James, and Mosi walked out of Westmoor Manor side by side.
In the distant sky, numerous figures were already rising into the air, shooting toward the enormous vortex like streaks of light.
"The Starlight Tournament is finally about to begin."
James had put away his usual frivolous and playful attitude. For once, a trace of solemnity appeared upon his face.
He knew exactly what this tournament represented.
The opponents they had encountered up until now, no matter how talented or powerful, were merely geniuses from a limited region.
But the individuals gathering in the Budelica Starfield were different.
They were monsters selected from eight entire starfields.
Every one of them would be an extraordinary prodigy standing above countless others.
"Looking forward to it."
Mosi unusually forced two words out of his throat.
Although his face remained as expressionless as ever, the faint battle intent radiating from his body was impossible to conceal.
Daniel glanced toward the enormous teleportation vortex in the sky.
His eyes shone with anticipation.
"Let’s go."
He took a single step into the void.
In the next instant, his figure disappeared into the distance.
"Let us meet the greatest prodigies this universe has to offer."
Two figures immediately followed behind him, shooting forward like meteors chasing the moon.
Together, the three of them flew straight toward the teleportation gate.
Toward the Budelica Starfield.
Toward the gathering storm of geniuses.
Toward the true stage of the universe.

chapters.title: Chapter 271 -271-The Tournament Draws Near, Thoughtstep
paragraphs: The instant Daniel passed through the teleportation gate, the world spun violently around him.
When his feet touched solid ground once more, an entirely unfamiliar world stretched out before his eyes.
There was something indescribably unusual about this place.
Whoosh! Whoosh!
James and Mosi appeared beside him almost simultaneously.
"A secret realm."
James swept his gaze across their surroundings. His eyes lit up, and a smile curled at the corners of his lips.
"And one personally created by a High Oracle-Grade expert, at that!"
"The space here is astonishingly stable... If I am not mistaken, this entire secret realm has been reinforced by layer upon layer of strengthening magic arrays."
"Yes."
Mosi, as sparing with words as ever, gave a brief confirmation.
Realization dawned upon Daniel.
No wonder he had felt that something was strange from the very moment he arrived.

This secret realm was even vaster than an ordinary Great World, and the MP in the air was so dense that it was almost viscous. A heavy, oppressive force permeated the atmosphere, as though an invisible giant hand were pressing firmly down upon his shoulders.
Having only just arrived, Daniel felt slightly uncomfortable at first.
After remaining here for a short while, however, he gradually adjusted to the pressure.
At this moment, all thirty experts from the Canaan Starfield’s Starlight Rankings had gathered in this place!
Daniel looked around.
They stood within a boundless range of mountains, one peak after another extending endlessly into the distance. The landscape was so vast that it seemed to have no end whatsoever.
"Truly breathtaking."
Even Daniel could not help feeling that his horizons had been broadened.
A place even larger than a Great World, with even more abundant MP, had actually been created from nothing by a High Oracle-Grade expert?!
"A secret realm is still not a life-bearing world in the end," James continued explaining. "A life-bearing world contains complete world laws. A secret realm does not."
"If a life-bearing world is compared to a perfectly balanced living organism, then a secret realm is merely an imperfect product that has been pushed to an extreme."
"The conditions required for a life-bearing world to form are unimaginably strict. Unless one reaches the level of an Eternal Sage, no existence can create a life-bearing world out of nothing."
Daniel’s heart stirred slightly when he heard the words Eternal Sage.
He still clearly remembered the human existence he had summoned back when he had forcibly initiated the World War!
That being had been able to roam through the Time River, travel between the past and the future, and wander among the countless universes.
Even now, the mere recollection of such power left Daniel deeply shaken.
"Mosi, your Law of Space will probably be somewhat restricted in this place."
Daniel cast Mosi a glance.

Mosi specialized in the Law of Space and had already achieved a certain level of accomplishment in it. However, the space within this secret realm had been heavily reinforced, so his abilities would almost certainly be affected.
"Mm."
Mosi frowned faintly.
At the same time—
[Ding! You have completed the first-stage mission.]
[Ding! You have obtained the mission reward: Mental State +10,000 points!]
Daniel’s eyes immediately brightened.
[Ding! You have sold Mental State ×10,000 points to the Doom Guild for 1 copper coin. Millionfold Boost activated!]
[Please select quality boost / quantity boost!]
"Quantity boost!"
[Congratulations! You have obtained Mental State +10,000,000,000 points!]
Listening to the notifications ringing beside his ears, Daniel felt immensely pleased.
His mission reward had finally fallen into his hands.
Now that he had accumulated such a massive amount of Mental State, he should be able to leap upward once again.
The moment he broke through, his strength would undoubtedly rise to an entirely new level!
All thirty experts from the Canaan Starfield’s Starlight Rankings had now arrived.
Just then, an Oracle-Grade expert from Gold-Grade Mountain slowly walked out from the void.
His steps were steady and imposing, as though each one carried the weight of an enormous mountain.
Every gaze immediately gathered upon him.
"I am Chanelle, a T7 Oracle-Grade!"
Chanelle’s voice was calm and unhurried, yet it rumbled clearly beside every person’s ears.

"The future of the Canaan Starfield has now been entrusted into your hands. You must spare neither effort nor life itself in winning greater benefits for the countless living beings of our starfield."
"A T7 Oracle-Grade! He’s actually a T7 Oracle-Grade!"
The experts on the Starlight Rankings instantly erupted into an uproar.
"Holy shit! If not for this tournament, I might never have had the opportunity to see a genuine T7 Oracle-Grade expert in my entire life!"
"A T7 Oracle-Grade! Even the ancestor of my race only reached T5!"
"This is a universe-level grand event, after all. Gold-Grade Mountain naturally had to dispatch a top expert to oversee matters."

"That’s right. Even if a T8 Oracle-Grade appeared, it wouldn’t be particularly surprising. The various starfields have accumulated grudges against one another for countless years. They cannot afford to let down their guard."
Chanelle continued, "The detailed rules of the tournament will be announced tomorrow. For today, remain here and rest while making your preparations."

Mountains rose and fell throughout this entire region, and every individual peak served as a secluded place for quiet cultivation.

Since the tournament had yet to begin and its rules would only be revealed the next day, the gathered experts quickly dispersed, each choosing a location to adjust their condition and make their final preparations.
"The tournament is right before us. We must prepare properly."
Daniel looked at the two companions standing beside him.
"I’ll go and familiarize myself with my current state first."
"Big Brother Faustus is right. I’ll go make some adjustments as well."
James nodded.
"Good."
Mosi remained as concise as ever.
This tournament was one in which life and death could be decided in a single instant!
More importantly, it concerned the fate of their entire starfield.
Not one of them dared to treat it lightly.

Daniel stepped inside.
"My current Rank is only Supreme-Grade, and I’ve been stuck at Level 400 with no way to advance."
Daniel silently considered his situation.
"Right now, I have more than ten billion Mental State points in my hands. If I can break through my Rank, my level should be able to rise along with it."
Having made his decision, he immediately began consuming his Mental State.
[Ding! You have consumed 2,000,000,000 Mental State points. Your Rank has advanced to—Demi-Sage!]
[Ding! You have comprehended Thoughtstep!]
Thoughtstep!
Daniel immediately stopped consuming Mental State.
The way he advanced now was different from before. He had to manually progress step by step.
Fortunately, his Exp Pool had already accumulated an enormous amount of experience!
[Notice: You have consumed experience points. Your current level has increased to Level 401!]
[Notice: You have consumed experience points. Your current level has increased to Level 480!]
[Notice: You have consumed experience points. Your current level has increased to Level 518!]
[Ding! You have not yet broken through your current Rank. You must break through before you can continue leveling up.]
Daniel blinked.
He had soared all the way to Level 518 in one breath.
That was even faster than completing a class-change mission!
Of course, what mattered even more was the immense leap in strength brought about by his Rank breakthrough.
Thoughtstep was extraordinarily powerful.
Daniel had fought against a fair number of Sages by now. Although he could currently instantly kill a Low-Grade Sage, that was not because Sages were weak.
It was because he himself was far too powerful.
He had become so strong that he had already exceeded the ordinary framework of power within this world.
The Sage Rank of an ordinary Mid-Grade Sage was already sufficient to contend evenly against his Divine Domain!
Their Sage Constitutions were extraordinarily special as well. Even when one possessed secret techniques, killing them in a single strike was extremely difficult.
More importantly, Sages possessed Thoughtstep.
No matter what action they took, their speed exceeded ordinary imagination!
Whether it was attacking, defending, reacting, or escaping, their thoughts seemed capable of transforming into action almost immediately.
And now...
Daniel possessed that ability as well.
By using Mental State to break through, he had comprehended Thoughtstep.
This was an enormous and unexpected delight.
His gaze fell upon a withered leaf drifting past the entrance of the building.
With a thought, he silently commanded it.
"Come here."
When Daniel lowered his eyes again, the leaf was already lying quietly in the center of his palm.
There had been no visible movement.
No pause.
No trace of the process between his thought and the result.
It was almost as if, the instant he had formed the intention, reality itself had obeyed.
"So this is... what Thoughtstep feels like!"
Daniel looked at the leaf in his palm, his eyes shining with excitement.
"This is wonderful!"
